# S2.2: Multiplex Edge Existence

<a id="s22-review"></a>
> Review state: **approved**, revision `S2.2-r2`, 2026-10-26.
> The user accepted the range-sampling finding and policy and directed the
> review onward. The API, source facts, and all 22 worked traces remain the
> approved design; runtime contracts, corpora, and training are unchanged.

## What this family should teach

Given two genes and a multiplex scope, establish whether any selected layer
records an edge, identify the supporting layers, or count them. These are
different requests. One observed edge can answer “any layer?”; “every layer,”
“only this layer,” and an exact total require complete coverage of that scope.

Keep each layer's representation intact. One undirected edge is one undirected
observation. Two oppositely directed edges in one TF layer remain two edges with
their own weights, but contribute only **one supporting layer**.

The original author proposal is retained: use a dedicated `get_edge_layers`
operation for a pair across layers. Extending `get_edge` to accept layer lists
was an alternative. This draft keeps S2.1's one-layer call stable and gives the
cross-layer operation explicit scope and completeness. The old positive-only
response is expanded to retain checked negatives and membership information.

The [S0/S1 lessons](#what-we-learned-from-s0-and-s1) motivate this change. S1 v9 exposed correct
facts paired with wrong continuation decisions and inconsistent result schemas;
v10's reviewed examples clarify the outer task. Here, matched examples hold
graph facts fixed while changing the request's scope or available evidence.
Retain current-turn reasoning, permitted retry limits, fixed structured answers,
and scoring that does not require exact summary prose. These are design lessons,
not measured S2 training gains.

## Sample the range of layer counts

<a id="s22-sampling"></a>
The user requested examples across the available range of layer counts, rather
than a few fixed choices. This is a **corpus sampling rule**. Each generated
question still has a concrete scope and, when applicable, a concrete bound.
The model must answer that request; it does not randomly change the scope or
limit at inference time.

Keep four quantities separate:

| Quantity | Meaning | Sampling rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `N` | Number of eligible layers in the pinned view and requested family/direction setting | Derive from the actual manifest; do not hard-code a historical layer count |
| `s` | Number of layers selected by this question | For explicit subsets, sample across `1..N` and vary the actual layer combinations |
| `h` | Number of selected layers that really satisfy the edge predicate | Sample across all attainable values within `0..s`, using verified pair/scope combinations |
| `k` | Bound requested for a first-K example | Sample across `1..s`, including `k<h`, `k=h`, and `k>h` where feasible |

An all-layer question still selects all eligible layers. A family-wide question
still selects the complete declared family. Vary `s` only when the question
explicitly requests a subset; do not turn an all-layer request into a random
partial scan. Explicit subset lists remain nonempty. A valid empty family
selection is its separate boundary case. The sampling range for `k` does not
change the API's acceptance of positive integer bounds.

The worked cases with zero, one, or several supporting layers illustrate
different reasoning situations. Their particular numbers and gene pairs are
not fixed templates or quotas for the training corpus. In particular, “several
layers” must span the attainable values above one, not repeatedly use two.
Sample layer identities and family combinations as well as counts; repeatedly
selecting the first `s` manifest entries would expose only a narrow set of scopes.
Render the selected set in manifest order after sampling it.

### Derive the count range from real data

Build the candidate inventory from the complete pinned source view and the
allowed pair pool, not only from the genes shown in this document. For each
scope and edge predicate, identify which supporting counts are actually
attainable. A number between the minimum and maximum is not automatically an
available outcome. Neither a missing endpoint nor an unavailable operation
belongs in the zero-support group.

A full-file audit of the current four-layer review view demonstrates the
difference. For `any_direction` across all four layers, using distinct unordered
pairs of the 19,033 multiplex nodes and excluding self-pairs:

| Supporting-layer count | Number of real pairs |
| ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 179,847,738 |
| 1 | 1,257,150 |
| 2 | 13,087 |
| 3 | 53 |
| 4 | 0 |

The attainable domain is `{0,1,2,3}`. Uniformly sampling gene pairs would mostly
produce zero-support examples and very rarely expose the three-layer cases.
For `both_directions` within the two TF layers, the attainable domain is only
`{0,1}`: brain contains 812 reciprocal distinct pairs, while CD4 contains none.
Do not manufacture a four-layer match or a two-layer reciprocal match to fill
an impossible count group.

These are reviewer calculations from the complete files, not supplied tool
statistics or a production sampling ceiling. The any-direction histogram sums
to 181,118,028 pairs, and its count-weighted positive total is 1,283,483 distinct
pair/layer memberships. That agrees with the source inventories after collapsing
reciprocal edges within a layer and excluding the five CD4 self-loops. Counts
include multiplex-node pairs whose endpoints are outside some selected layers,
under the approved membership rule. They do not certify every pair's registry
status or eligibility for a future split; recompute the feasible groups after
applying the approved candidate and split rules.

The future production view must be independently pinned and source-verified.
Recompute its ranges from that view. Do not limit it to these four review layers
or copy this histogram to another snapshot.

### Choose counts first, then varied real examples

For the new corpus, establish the allowed source pools and splits before
sampling. Group related pair, direction, scope, and evidence variants together
to avoid splitting near-duplicates between training and evaluation. Preserve
existing frozen panels and published corpora.

Use a seeded schedule that covers every attainable count in the selected
training pools. As the default, give attainable count values equal sampling
weight, then draw real pair/scope candidates within each group. Vary explicit
scope sizes across their full eligible range and vary bounded `k` values too.
Enforce the actual feasibility constraints between `s`, `h`, and `k`; do not
sample an impossible combination and alter graph facts to make it fit.

Within each count group, vary gene pairs, layer identities and families,
direction predicates, direct/workflow framing, evidence position, and
complete/partial context. Keep content selection independent of wording-bank
size. Track distinct pairs and scopes so a rare group does not appear diverse
merely because one example was repeated under many wordings. Record the sampling
weights, seed, source pins, available candidates, selected counts, and omissions.

Cover attainable values across the built corpus; do not require every minibatch
to contain every value or claim that every combination has been illustrated.
Report both marginal count coverage and coverage of feasible combinations.
If the corpus budget cannot cover the requested range, expose that gap for
review rather than silently keeping only small counts. Likewise, use actual
tokenizer/context checks for large scopes. If complete examples cannot fit,
review the representation or context budget before building them; do not truncate
an all-layer answer or silently exclude the upper range.

The fully checked count may guide candidate selection, but it is not extra
model-visible evidence. An existence or bounded trace must still report an
unknown total when its visible observations do not establish the exact count.
Record natural data frequencies separately from the sampled frequencies and
report new evaluation results by scope size and supporting count. Count coverage
is a data-design check, not a guarantee that the model has learned the graph.

## Proposed tool and result

<a id="s22-interface"></a>
Every call supplies all six arguments:

```text
get_edge_layers({
  multiplex_id: string,
  gene_ids: [canonical_id_A, canonical_id_B],
  layer_scope: {kind: layers | all, layer_ids: string[], layer_family: string | null},
  edge_query: any_direction | source_to_target | both_directions,
  mode: complete | top_k | exists,
  top_k: positive integer | null
})
```

The multiplex, graph version, and manifest must be known. Resolve identities
with the approved S1 rules, preserving raw lookup inputs, candidate lists, and
selection evidence. Require two distinct canonical IDs. The edge tool checks
both multiplex memberships; canonical IDs do not require a separate membership
call. Unknown identity, missing scope, and invalid pairs use the diagnostic
rules below rather than fabricated graph negatives.

### Scope and direction are explicit

`layer_scope` uses the shared selector. An `all` selector with no family means
every registered layer; `all` with `tf_target` means only that family's layers.
An explicit layer list is deduplicated and ordered by the registered manifest.
Show that resolved list in coverage. Completing a subset says nothing about
excluded layers. A valid family with no layers selects an empty scope; after
membership checks, its complete answer is false with an exact count of zero.
An unknown family or layer is a scope error, not an empty selection.

| `edge_query` | What makes a layer support the pair |
| --- | --- |
| `any_direction` | An undirected edge, or at least one directed orientation |
| `source_to_target` | The directed edge from the first input ID to the second |
| `both_directions` | Both directed edges, each retaining its own weight |

The last two predicates require a selected scope of directed representations.
If an explicit request includes an undirected layer, return
`invalid_input/DIRECTION_UNAVAILABLE`. Do not drop that layer silently, count
it as a negative, or reinterpret one undirected edge as two directed edges.
When the user asks about “directed layers,” use the visible manifest to select
them explicitly. A TF family filter is sufficient only when its resolved
layers are actually directed in this version; the family name is not proof.

Preserve `[A,B]` as the reference order in the aggregate and tool arguments.
Within observations, directed pairs retain `[source,target]`; undirected pairs
are canonicalized by ID. For `any_direction` and `both_directions`, reversing
the reference order does not change which layers qualify, but must not reverse
the actual recorded source/target roles. A `source_to_target` query changes
meaning when the input order changes.

### Match the retrieval to the request

| Mode | Intended request | Completion rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `complete` | Every supporting layer or an exact layer count | Check the complete selected scope; `top_k:null` |
| `top_k` | First K supporting layers in manifest order | Check through the Kth match, or exhaust the scope; require positive `top_k` |
| `exists` | Whether any selected layer qualifies | A witness settles true; false requires the complete scope; `top_k:null` |

`top_k` orders **layers by the manifest**, never by weights across incompatible
layer scales. There is no default cap. This draft does not paginate the batch
operation: `next_cursor` is null on successful collection results, and a complete
request must finish or report an error. To extend a saved bounded scan, request
its unchecked layer subset and combine the evidence. Cursor-based pagination
would require an explicit later interface change.

An existence witness need not be the first match. A fresh existence scan can
visit layers in manifest order, but saved positive evidence from a later layer
can answer the Boolean immediately. It cannot answer “first matching layer”
while earlier layers remain unchecked. A first-K answer needs every preceding
potentially qualifying layer checked; merely knowing K positives is insufficient.

The tool returns `{status, provenance, result}`. The fixed ordinary result is:

```text
result: {
  multiplex_id: string,
  gene_ids: [A, B],
  layer_scope: LayerScope,
  edge_query: any_direction | source_to_target | both_directions,
  mode: complete | top_k | exists,
  edge_exists_any_layer: boolean | null,
  layer_results: LayerResult[] | null,
  supporting_layer_ids: string[] | null,
  supporting_layer_count: nonnegative integer | null,
  missing_gene_ids: string[],
  coverage: {
    operation: "layer_edge_checks",
    requested_layer_ids: string[],
    checked_layer_ids: string[],
    unchecked_layer_ids: string[]
  },
  collection: Collection | null
}

LayerResult: {
  layer_id: string,
  directed: boolean,
  edge_exists: boolean,
  edges: [{gene_ids: [id_1, id_2], weight: number}, ...],
  not_in_layer_gene_ids: string[],
  coverage: {
    operation: "edge_checks",
    requested_pairs: [[id_1, id_2], ...],
    checked_pairs: [[id_1, id_2], ...],
    unchecked_pairs: [[id_1, id_2], ...]
  }
}
```

`Collection` keeps the approved fields: `mode`, `returned_count`, `total_count`,
`complete`, and `next_cursor`. Its mode is `complete` or `top_k`. An `exists`
result has `collection:null` because it answers a Boolean and makes no first-K
claim. A missing prerequisite also has `collection:null`.

`supporting_layer_ids` is the manifest-ordered list of checked rows whose
`edge_exists` predicate is true. Count each ID once. `returned_count` is the
length of that list. `supporting_layer_count` and `total_count` give an exact
selected-scope total only when all layer predicates are known; otherwise they
are null. The returned list still supplies a lower bound. `complete:true`
requires the full supporting list and the same known total. A completed bounded
or existence request may leave layers unchecked without being an error.

`layer_results` retains every checked layer, including negatives. Its `edges`
contains observed positive edges only. For each checked ordered pair, absence
from that row's `edges` is a checked negative. An unchecked pair cannot be treated
as negative. Layer-absence lists are sorted subsets of the queried multiplex
nodes and are independent of edge omission. A negative layer predicate with an
empty membership-absence list means both endpoints were checked as layer members.

Two coverage levels answer different questions. Outer coverage says whether
each layer's requested predicate is settled. Inner coverage says which edge
orientations are known. One saved forward positive can settle `any_direction`
in that layer while leaving its reverse unchecked; one checked negative can
settle `both_directions`. Neither supplies a full directional pattern. When
the user also asks for all directions or weights, require the corresponding
inner coverage before presenting those details as complete.

A fresh batch lookup returns the complete requested orientation set for each
visited layer: one unordered pair for an undirected layer, one ordered pair
for `source_to_target`, or both ordered pairs otherwise. Directed observations
are in reference-forward/reverse order. A result derived from saved evidence
may have partial inner coverage when it still fully answers the requested
predicate. Clearly explain that inference and retain its actual evidence.

### Status, partial results, and provenance

| Outcome | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Some layer qualifies and the requested retrieval is complete | `resolved`; stop or continue from the outer task |
| Every selected layer is checked and none qualifies | `resolved/false`, empty supporting list, exact count zero |
| Queried multiplex node is outside a layer | That layer can be a checked negative; retain its membership-absence IDs |
| An endpoint is outside the multiplex | `not_found/defer`; layer predicates, lists, and counts remain unavailable |
| Required remaining-scope lookup fails without recovery | `error/defer`; retain supported earlier observations and unchecked layers |

For multiplex absence, check both endpoint memberships. `missing_gene_ids`
records the missing IDs; `edge_exists_any_layer`, `layer_results`,
`supporting_layer_ids`, and `supporting_layer_count` are null. All selected
layers remain unchecked for `layer_edge_checks`. The evidence licenses the
membership finding, not a negative edge scan.

Use the approved failure shape: `failed_tool`, `error_code`, exact failed
`arguments`, attributed `partial_results`, and layer coverage for the original
request. A partial positive cannot complete an exhaustive list. Failed calls
have empty evidence channels and add no graph observations under this proposed
atomic batch protocol. Preserve saved records and independently successful
earlier subset calls; do not invent evidence for internal work that an error
did not return. Streaming partial results from inside a failed batch would
require a separately reviewed runtime extension.

Retry only when explicitly allowed, with identical arguments, and stop on
success. A recovered remaining-scope scan is combined with prior evidence;
task scope then determines stop or continue. Exhaustion defers for backend
availability, without automatically demanding different gene names.

Keep list-valued registry and graph provenance. A bounded or existence scan's
graph scope names only its checked layers. An exhaustive record may use its
requested scope, including a family selector. Never use `all` as evidence that
an incomplete scan checked everything. Missing-membership evidence may describe
the multiplex scope while edge coverage remains explicitly unchecked. Deduplicate
identical records; reject conflicting evidence IDs or graph versions.

Combine independent subset results only when pair, version, representation, and
edge predicate are compatible. Rebuild the final scope, coverage, collection,
and exact total from their union; keep every supporting evidence record. Mark
these as model calculations over supplied observations, rather than inventing
a tool response or new acquisition ID. Saved richer evidence can answer a
narrower question: project a complete record into `mode:exists` without losing
its supported facts or making new calls.

### Other blocked requests and claim limits

Use the S2.1 diagnostic protocol, with this S2.2 request shape:

```text
result: {
  issue_code: string,
  request: {
    genes: string[],
    multiplex_id: string | null,
    layer_scope: LayerScope | null,
    edge_query: string | null,
    mode: string | null,
    top_k: integer | null
  },
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...]
}
```

Preserve the original gene strings and any registry partials. Missing scope,
invalid pairs, unresolved or missing identities, and unknown multiplexes/layers
retain the S2.1 status/issue-code meanings. Add `INVALID_SELECTION` for unknown
family names, unsupported edge-query/mode values, or invalid top-k combinations;
use `invalid_input/defer` without fabricated graph evidence. Known local
rejections need no call. A tool-detected rejection returns
`{status, provenance:{registry:[],graph:[]}, result:{issue_code,arguments}}`,
where arguments exactly match the rejected call. The final diagnostic retains
the original request and any valid earlier results. Full registry-selection and
remaining diagnostic traces are future corpus requirements.

Ordinary answers omit claim cards. A complete negative supports only absence
of the requested edge predicate in the checked scope and version. In particular,
no reverse edge does not mean no forward edge; no supporting TF layer does not
mean no PPI edge; no edge does not rule out a longer path. One reciprocal layer
does not prove a feedback mechanism, and several layers do not automatically
represent independent biological confirmations. Apply the same S1/S2 claim
meanings wherever the actual evidence is identical.

Revision `S2.2-r2`, 2026-10-26, is **approved**. The user approved S2.1 and
directed the review to advance. Its accepted behavior and source view are
retained; this family adds a proposed cross-layer batch interface and examples.
The user subsequently required sampling across the available count range.
R6 adds that corpus policy and a full-source count-domain audit. The tool
semantics and all 22 worked traces remain unchanged; no corpus sampler is
implemented or run in this document-review phase. The user accepted the
finding and directed the review onward, approving S2.2 and its sampling policy.

| Decision | State | Accepted behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G1 — task-specific retrieval | approved (2026-10-26) | Complete list/count, first-K layer list, and existence Boolean have distinct completion rules |
| G2 — direction across layers | approved (2026-10-26) | Preserve native edges and weights; explicit directed scopes for ordered/both-direction predicates |
| G3 — results and counting | approved (2026-10-26) | Retain checked negatives, inner and outer coverage, unique supporting IDs, and unknown versus exact totals |
| G4 — reuse and failures | approved (2026-10-26) | Reuse valid observations, scan remaining scopes, retain attributed partial results, and apply accepted retry/status rules |
| G5 — sources and coverage | approved (2026-10-26) | Preserve all seven original roles with real facts; add fifteen contrasts and mark remaining coverage honestly |
| G6 — range sampling | approved (2026-10-26) | Derive attainable counts from real sources, sample scope sizes/support counts/bounds across the range, vary layer combinations, and audit gaps without fabricating outcomes |

# S2.3: Layer-Specific Direct Neighbors

<a id="s23-review"></a>
> Review state: **approved**, revision `S2.3-r1`; human approval recorded in
> `S2-design-r8`, 2026-10-26.
> S2.2 and its range-sampling policy are approved. This family applies the
> accepted neighbor interface, membership rules, direction, and collection
> semantics to real examples. Runtime and published corpora remain unchanged.

## What this family should teach

List the direct neighbors of one gene in one layer, with their recorded weights,
or return a requested strongest-K prefix. For directed layers, distinguish
incoming from outgoing neighbors. Decide whether saved evidence is sufficient,
whether more pages are needed, and whether the result completes the user's
question or a step in a larger workflow.

The original author concerns about large lists, ordering, and duplicate rows
remain relevant. Replace the proposed default cap with explicit bounded
requests and transport pagination. A runtime page size must not silently turn
“every neighbor” into “the first few.” Runtime lists have unique neighbor IDs;
combining overlapping pages still requires deduplicating identical entries.

S1's measured scope and schema errors motivate matched direct/workflow cases,
consistent result fields, and reasoning about what remains required. Retain
current-turn reasoning and runtime-authorized retry limits. Score structured
facts and decisions without exact prose matching. The [shared lessons](#what-we-learned-from-s0-and-s1)
are the evidence for these design choices, not a claim of measured S2 gains.

## Operation and exact results

<a id="s23-interface"></a>
Use the neighbor interface already introduced in the shared rules:

```text
get_neighbors({
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: string,
  gene_id: canonical_gene_id,
  direction: in | out | undirected,
  mode: complete | top_k,
  top_k: positive integer | null,
  cursor: string | null
})
```

Every argument is explicit. `complete` requires `top_k:null`; `top_k` mode
requires a positive integer. Start a new selection with `cursor:null`. Resolve
symbols and noncanonical inputs under S1's rules unless exact authoritative
context already supplies the identity. A canonical input does not need a
separate membership call: the neighbor tool checks multiplex and layer
membership. Keep scope and version fixed throughout a traversal.

| Direction | Meaning of a returned neighbor N for queried gene Q |
| --- | --- |
| `out` | Q → N is recorded |
| `in` | N → Q is recorded |
| `undirected` | The layer records an unordered Q–N edge |

Per-layer metadata must support the requested representation. Do not infer
incoming roles from an undirected layer, choose outgoing from a TF tag alone,
or reverse an incoming observation to answer an outgoing question.

A successful tool response is `{status, provenance, result}`. Keep the approved
ordinary result shape, including `gene_id` rather than legacy `query_gene_id`:

```text
result: {
  gene_id: canonical_gene_id,
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: string,
  direction: in | out | undirected,
  neighbors: [{gene_id: canonical_gene_id, weight: number}, ...] | null,
  missing_gene_ids: string[],
  not_in_layer_gene_ids: string[],
  collection: {
    mode: complete | top_k,
    returned_count: nonnegative integer,
    total_count: nonnegative integer | null,
    complete: boolean,
    next_cursor: string | null
  } | null
}
```

There is no second ambiguous `neighbor_count` or `truncated_to_top_k` field.
`returned_count` counts rows in this response or final accumulated answer.
`total_count` is the full number of distinct neighbors for this gene, layer,
version, and direction, if known. It is not the requested K. Copy supplied
totals; never replace an unknown total with the returned row count unless a
complete traversal establishes that count.

Sort by descending numeric weight, then ascending canonical neighbor ID.
Return exactly `min(K, total)` entries when the bounded traversal finishes.
Tied weights do not authorize extra rows beyond K. There is no cross-layer or
cross-direction weight aggregation. Source precision is retained.

Preserve a source self-loop by including the query ID once in the applicable
directional list. It may appear in both incoming and outgoing views of the
same self-edge; that does not create two distinct edges. The neighbor count is
distinct-ID cardinality under this convention, not automatically an undirected
graph-theoretic degree that counts a loop twice. Requests to exclude self-loops
would need an explicitly defined filter; no silent exclusion is introduced here.

### Membership and task completion

| What the operation establishes | Result and continuation |
| --- | --- |
| Present node, requested list or bounded prefix obtained | `resolved`; stop for a direct question, continue its stated workflow |
| Present node, zero neighbors in this direction | `resolved`, `neighbors:[]`, known total zero, empty membership-absence lists |
| Multiplex node absent from this layer | `resolved`, `neighbors:[]`, known total zero, query ID in `not_in_layer_gene_ids` |
| Query ID absent from the multiplex | `not_found/defer`, `neighbors:null`, `collection:null`, query ID in `missing_gene_ids` |
| Required lookup/page fails without recovery | `error/defer`, attributed supported partial results, no invented complete list |

This explicitly repairs legacy S2.3.5: layer absence is a completed neighbor
operation with an empty result and an explicit reason. It is different from a
present isolated node. An empty outgoing list establishes zero outgoing
neighbors; it does not establish zero incoming neighbors or full isolation.
A multiplex-missing ID leaves the operation unavailable, rather than empty.

Ordinary neighbor answers omit claim cards. Returned neighbors and weights
support scoped graph observations, including directed TF roles when the source
preserves them. They do not establish activation/repression sign, causality,
expression, or observations in other layers or versions. A top-K omission is
not absence. Keep the same claim meanings as S2.1 and the calibration families.

## Complete lists, bounded lists, and pages

<a id="s23-pagination"></a>
An unqualified full-list request such as “list the neighbors” uses complete
mode. A requested strongest-K list uses that explicit bound. The transport can
split either traversal into pages, but pagination does not change the requested
selection.

1. Start at the initial null cursor, or reuse a visible valid prefix of that
   same traversal.
2. Follow each returned cursor exactly, preserving gene, layer, version,
   direction, mode, and K. The cursor is opaque; never construct or edit it.
3. Retain the observations and evidence from every page used. Deduplicate
   identical neighbor/weight entries and preserve the global rank order.
4. End when the traversal's cursor is null. For complete mode, only accumulation
   from the initial page through exhaustion establishes the complete list.

A page's `complete` flag describes that page's coverage of the full directional
neighbor set. The last page may still have `complete:false`, because earlier
pages contain other neighbors. Its null cursor ends the traversal; it does not
turn that page alone into the whole collection. In a final complete answer,
the accumulated `returned_count` and known `total_count` agree, `complete` is
true, and `next_cursor` is null. If no page supplies a total, count the unique
entries in the exhausted complete traversal and identify this as a model
calculation over the supplied observations.

For top-K mode, null cursor ends the bounded retrieval. The final answer can be
resolved with `complete:false` when K is smaller than the full list, even if
`total_count` is unknown. If fewer than K neighbors exist, exhaustion returns
all available entries and can establish a complete collection. Successful
bounded retrieval must return the exact requested ranked prefix or establish
that the list is exhausted; a shorter intermediate page is insufficient.

Changing a saved bounded request to a complete request starts at `cursor:null`.
A cursor does not transfer between different modes, bounds, directions, genes,
layers, or versions. A usable saved complete-mode prefix can continue with its
actual cursor. Conflicting weights for one neighbor, inconsistent non-null
totals, or an invalid cursor chain are contract/data faults; reject those as
gold traces rather than silently choosing a convenient result.

The page boundaries and cursor tokens in the worked examples are proposed
harness behavior over real neighbor records, not captures from a deployed
runtime. Single-row pages keep the complete traces readable. Production page
sizes and context budgets must be reviewed separately from the logical list
size; neither imposes a hidden cap on an all-neighbors request.

### When context is sufficient

| Visible evidence | What the model can do |
| --- | --- |
| Complete matching directional list, including membership and version | Answer every-neighbor request without a call |
| Complete matching list, smaller K requested | Derive the exact ranked prefix, keep the known full total, and retain its evidence |
| Matching ranked prefix already covers the requested K | Answer that bounded question without a call |
| Truncated list, every neighbor or a larger prefix requested | Obtain the missing selection; a complete query starts at a null cursor |
| Complete-mode page prefix with valid cursor | Continue that same traversal and accumulate pages |
| Correct gene but wrong layer, version, or direction | Obtain matching evidence; do not reuse incompatible adjacency |
| A single incident edge | Supports that entry, but not a complete or strongest-K list unless independent evidence proves the required ranking/coverage |

The source catalogue and count-domain audits are reviewer references. They do
not supply hidden neighbor entries, totals, registry mappings, or cursor state
to the model in a trace.

## Incoming and outgoing lists together

<a id="s23-both-directions"></a>
On a directed layer, an unqualified request for all neighbors or incident
connections means both incoming and outgoing connections. This is a valid
discovery question, not missing source/target input. Retrieve both lists and
keep the directions separate. A request that names only incoming or outgoing
uses the ordinary result above.

`both` is a **compound final-answer direction**, not a new `get_neighbors`
argument. Use two ordinary directional operations as needed, or reuse sufficient
evidence for either side. When neither is supplied, retrieve incoming first
and outgoing second. Do not perform a second lookup merely to reconfirm a
membership finding that already establishes layer absence in both directions.

```text
result: {
  gene_id: canonical_gene_id,
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: string,
  direction: both,
  incoming: NeighborResult | null,
  outgoing: NeighborResult | null,
  coverage: {
    operation: "neighbor_directions",
    requested_directions: [in, out],
    checked_directions: direction[],
    unchecked_directions: direction[]
  }
}
```

`NeighborResult` is the ordinary result shape. A direction is checked when its
requested collection is supplied: every neighbor in complete mode, or the
required prefix/exhaustion in bounded mode. This is separate from whether that
direction's full collection has `complete:true`. Order coverage lists as
incoming then outgoing. Each requested direction appears exactly once in the
checked or unchecked list. A resolved compound result requires both requested
directions checked. Keep their evidence union; do not add their counts to claim
a distinct combined-neighbor count, since one neighbor can occur on both sides.

If an endpoint is missing from the multiplex, keep the observed unavailable
`NeighborResult`, leave an unqueried side null, mark both directions unchecked,
and return `not_found/defer`. The shared prerequisite makes another lookup
unnecessary. A known layer absence instead permits both directional empty
results to be derived from that observation; explain the derivation and reuse
its evidence without inventing a second tool response.

“Top K incoming and top K outgoing” can use the same compound shape, applying K
separately to each side. “Top K incident neighbors overall” requires a rule for
comparing or combining two directional weights. That ranking is not defined
here: use the diagnostic below to request the missing ranking specification,
rather than inventing max, sum, or another aggregation. A full incident list
does not need that extra ranking rule because the two lists remain separate.

## Failures and other blocked requests

For an unrecovered required backend failure, use the accepted failure shape:
`failed_tool`, `error_code`, exact failed `arguments`, attributed
`partial_results`, and `coverage`. A failed call adds no new evidence. Retain
registry observations, valid saved lists, and successful pages actually used.

For one directional neighbor traversal, `coverage` is null; partial-page
collection metadata supplies the available coverage information. Do not invent
IDs or a total count for unknown future pages. For a compound incoming/outgoing
request, use `neighbor_directions` coverage. A partially retrieved side remains
unchecked until its requested collection is complete, while its successful
pages are preserved as attributed records.

Retry only when the runtime explicitly allows another attempt. Repeat the
identical failed call, including its cursor. After success, stop retrying and
finish any still-required traversal; then derive stop/continue from the outer
request. After exhaustion, defer for the real backend blocker. An empty list,
layer absence, or a completed bounded result is not a reason to retry.

The family-specific diagnostic uses the approved protocol. `NeighborArguments`
means the exact seven-field `get_neighbors` argument object shown above.

```text
result: {
  issue_code: string,
  request: {
    gene: string,
    multiplex_id: string | null,
    layer_id: string | null,
    direction: in | out | undirected | both | null,
    mode: complete | top_k | null,
    top_k: integer | null,
    cursor: string | null
  },
  rejected_arguments: NeighborArguments | null,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...]
}
```

Preserve the original gene text and supported registry partials. Identity
ambiguity or absence, missing scope, unknown registered scope, and invalid gene
inputs keep the S2.1 status meanings. A known direction/representation mismatch
is `invalid_input/DIRECTION_UNAVAILABLE`. Invalid mode/K combinations or an
invalid/stale cursor are `invalid_input/INVALID_SELECTION` or
`invalid_input/INVALID_CURSOR`, respectively. Preserve any valid earlier page
records without presenting their partial list as complete. A runtime rejection
returns the shared empty-provenance `{issue_code, arguments}` result. Copy the
exact seven rejected tool arguments, including its cursor, into
`rejected_arguments`. The original request keeps its original gene text and
requested selection; it may differ from the resolved tool arguments. A known
local rejection has `rejected_arguments:null`. Do not fabricate an
evidence-bearing partial record for an unsupported rejection.

A bounded request with no K is `invalid_input/MISSING_LIMIT`. A request for
one strongest-K ranking across both directions without an aggregation rule is
`ambiguous/NEIGHBOR_RANKING_AMBIGUOUS`. Explain the actual missing specification.
Known local rejections need no call; unavailable facts must be obtained rather
than guessed. Full traces for remaining diagnostic and identity branches are
explicit future corpus requirements.

## Real examples and sampling across the available range

<a id="s23-sampling"></a>
Use the same complete pinned source files and graph version. These selected
examples are short illustrations, not limits on the production sampling range.

| Source-backed example | Verified neighbor facts |
| --- | --- |
| DEFB124, PPI | Complete list: PGRMC1 at 0.646504358855666, then NCK2 at 0.606202588120059 |
| HMGN1, CD4 | Outgoing: LINC00486 at 0.866, then HFM1 at 0.818; incoming: empty |
| CDC27, CD4 | Incoming: CREBBP at 1; outgoing: empty; the node is present |
| SLC6A7 / CCT8L1P | SLC6A7 is outside PPI but in the multiplex; CCT8L1P is outside the multiplex |
| MROH8, PPI | Two neighbors, ENSG00000129514 and ENSG00000164068, both 0.292292292292292; source lines 312899–312900 |
| BCL6, CD4 | Incoming: self only, weight 1, source line 157; 731 outgoing neighbors |

The two additional query identities are verified against the pinned registry
index and original GTF: MROH8 is ENSG00000101353 and BCL6 is ENSG00000113916.
Their GTF gene rows are at lines 10,075,096 and 2,165,137 respectively. Model
traces using only canonical IDs must not introduce these symbols unless their
identity evidence is visible.

Carry forward the approved [range-sampling policy](#s22-sampling). For neighbors,
derive the attainable distinct-neighbor counts separately for each eligible
layer and direction. Sample count values, then real genes within those groups;
vary K over the eligible range rather than teaching a few fixed bounds. Include
K below, equal to, and above the available count wherever feasible. All-neighbor
questions still require all neighbors. Layer absence and multiplex absence are
separate cases, not extra examples of present-node degree zero.

A full-source audit gives the following domains among actual layer members.
Self-loops contribute one neighbor in the applicable direction:

| Layer / direction | Observed count range | Members with zero | Distinct attainable counts |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PPI / undirected | 1–2940 | 0 | 812 |
| Coexpression / undirected | 1–218 | 0 | 189 |
| Brain TF / outgoing | 0–1152 | 10,621 | 431 |
| Brain TF / incoming | 0–45 | 269 | 44 |
| CD4 TF / outgoing | 0–1673 | 5,784 | 27 |
| CD4 TF / incoming | 0–27 | 17 | 16 |

These ranges contain gaps. For example, brain incoming counts 1 and 40 do not
occur. Sample the observed values after applying candidate/split rules, rather
than every integer between the minimum and maximum. Choose positive K values
across the relevant layer-node range, with separate coverage of the feasible
K/count relationships. Recompute domains for new source views; the four review
layers and these query genes do not define the production ceiling.

The audit uses complete source endpoint sets. Histogram sizes equal layer-node
counts; summed neighbor counts equal edge-row totals for each directed side,
and twice the edge-row totals for these loop-free undirected layers. These are
reviewer calculations, not extra model-visible statistics. Vary gene/layer/
direction, framing, evidence position, and pagination independently where the
data allow. Pin sampler policy and seed, preserve frozen panels, and report
count coverage and distinct example diversity. Apply actual tokenizer/context
checks to large complete results; pagination alone does not make an oversized
final answer fit. Resolve that representation/budget issue before corpus
construction instead of silently dropping large counts or clipping full lists.

ranked prefix. Order weights descending, then canonical neighbor IDs ascending.

all-incident-neighbors request composes incoming and outgoing lists separately.

all pages required by the actual request; a page boundary is not an answer cap.

operations. Retain current-turn reasoning and use only authorized retries.

check_multiplex_membership, get_edge, get_neighbors, and get_edge_layers.

# S2.4: Multiplex Direct Neighbors

<a id="s24-review"></a>
> **Review state: approved.** The user approved S2.4 at R9 and M2’s
> [empty-family alignment with S2.2](#s25-empty-family-alignment) at R11,
> 2026-10-27. All worked traces remain approved. These interfaces describe
> a future contract, not a runtime change.

## What this family should teach

Given one gene and a set of layers, report each direct neighbor once and show
every selected layer that connects it to the query. Preserve each layer's own
weight and direction. A neighbor supported by two layers is still one neighbor;
two reciprocal edges in one layer still constitute one supporting layer.

For example, the real PPI and coexpression files both connect MFRP to C1QTNF5.
That gives one neighbor with two supports, at different source weights. In a
different example, CDC27 has three undirected coexpression neighbors and one
incoming CD4 TF neighbor. Its map must preserve those different relationships.
The [source facts](#s24-sources) below make these examples auditable.

The [S0/S1 lessons](#what-we-learned-from-s0-and-s1) apply directly: interpret the
outer request, reuse evidence that actually answers it, and keep wording from
predicting the outcome. A successful lookup can finish a direct question or
complete a step in a larger workflow. Neither the presence of context nor the
word “next” alone determines continuation. Give the reasoning needed to explain
the evidence and decision; do not add length for its own sake.

## Scope, direction, and ordering

<a id="s24-semantics"></a>
Resolve identities and registered scopes using the approved S1/S2 conventions.
Keep raw lookup text, candidate selection, layer grammars, and family mappings.
An already canonical ID does not require a redundant symbol lookup. Layer
membership and graph version must come from the declared view.

Use the same typed `layer_scope` as S2.2. An explicit subset is deduplicated and
ordered by the manifest. An all-layer request expands to every manifest layer;
an all-family request expands to every registered layer of that family. Do not
silently replace either with a small example subset. Unknown scope and an empty
explicit selection use the existing scope/selection diagnostics. A valid
family with no registered layers selects an empty scope,
as in S2.2. After the multiplex-membership prerequisite is satisfied, return a
resolved empty map with count zero and empty layer-coverage lists. This records
an empty selection, not a measured absence from actual layers. Unknown family
or layer identifiers remain diagnostics. This
[alignment](#s25-empty-family-alignment) was approved on 2026-10-27.

| Requested direction | Meaning and precondition |
| --- | --- |
| `incident` | All native connections: undirected adjacency in an undirected layer, and incoming plus outgoing edges in a directed layer |
| `in` | Only edges from the neighbor to the query; every selected representation must be directed |
| `out` | Only edges from the query to the neighbor; every selected representation must be directed |
| `undirected` | Undirected adjacency only; every selected representation must be undirected |

“All neighbors” means `incident` unless the request selects a particular
orientation. Mixed directed and undirected layers are therefore valid for an
incident map. An incoming-only request over a mixed scope is blocked by the
representation mismatch; do not silently omit the undirected layers or reverse
their edges. This multiplex selector extends the interface for this family;
it does not add `incident` to the single-layer S2.3 tool.

Sort neighbor rows by canonical gene ID. Within each row, sort supporting layers
by manifest order. In a directed support, list incoming then outgoing edges
relative to the query, preserving each source/target pair and weight. A self-loop
is one stored edge: emit it once, in the incoming position when both orientations
are requested. In an undirected support, sort the two endpoint IDs. Never sort
directed endpoints to make them look undirected. Do not sort neighbor rows by
one layer's weight or combine weights from different sources.

## Proposed call and result

<a id="s24-interface"></a>
All seven arguments are explicit. The runtime binds the active graph version
to each acquisition and cursor, as in S2.3.

```text
get_neighbor_layers({
  multiplex_id: string,
  gene_id: canonical gene ID,
  layer_scope: LayerScope,
  direction: incident | in | out | undirected,
  mode: complete | top_k,
  top_k: positive integer | null,
  cursor: string | null
})
```

`complete` asks for every unique neighbor and requires `top_k:null`. `top_k`
returns the first K unique neighbor IDs in the stated canonical ordering; it
does **not** mean the strongest K neighbors. Require a positive explicit K and
make that selection clear in the request. Return exactly `min(K, total)` rows
over the completed traversal. An unqualified request for “strongest multiplex
neighbors” needs a ranking rule before this tool can answer it.

**Every returned neighbor row must contain its complete support in the selected
scope**, even in a bounded result or on an intermediate page. A runtime cannot
merge S2.3's independently weight-ranked top-K lists and present them as this
operation. Those truncated lists can omit both the required canonical-ID
neighbors and supporting layers. No default layer cap or neighbor cap is permitted.

Resolved and membership-not-found responses use `{status, provenance, result}`.
Ordinary final answers copy this fixed result or derive the same shape from
sufficient compatible observations:

```text
result: {
  query_gene_id: canonical gene ID,
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_scope: LayerScope,
  direction: incident | in | out | undirected,
  layer_results: [
    {layer_id: string, directed: boolean,
     not_in_layer_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...]}, ...
  ] | null,
  neighbors: [
    {
      gene_id: canonical neighbor ID,
      supporting_layers: [
        {layer_id: string, directed: boolean,
         edges: [{gene_ids: [source, target], weight: number}, ...]}, ...
      ],
      supporting_layer_count: positive integer
    }, ...
  ] | null,
  unique_neighbor_count: nonnegative integer | null,
  missing_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  layers_without_gene: [layer ID, ...] | null,
  coverage: {
    operation: layer_neighbor_maps,
    requested_layer_ids: [layer ID, ...],
    checked_layer_ids: [layer ID, ...],
    unchecked_layer_ids: [layer ID, ...]
  },
  collection: {
    mode: complete | top_k,
    returned_count: nonnegative integer,
    total_count: nonnegative integer | null,
    complete: boolean,
    next_cursor: string | null
  } | null
}
```

For undirected supports, `gene_ids` contains the canonicalized unordered pair
described above. A neighbor's `supporting_layer_count` is the length of its
supporting-layer list, not its edge count. `unique_neighbor_count` and
`collection.total_count` both refer to the full unique-neighbor collection for
this gene, scope, and direction; they must agree, including when both are null.
`returned_count` describes only the rows actually returned in that response.
Do not sum per-layer counts to obtain a union count.

`layer_results` includes every selected layer in manifest order and records
whether the query is absent from that layer. `layers_without_gene` lists exactly
those absences. These fields separate a present node with no outgoing neighbors
from a node absent from the layer. They are not per-layer neighbor lists.

**Coverage and completeness answer different questions.** A checked layer has
been evaluated for the requested map selection, including membership and all
applicable support for every returned row. A resolved bounded result or page
therefore has every selected layer checked. That does not say that every
neighbor row has been returned; `collection` supplies that information. A
completed empty map requires an exhaustive negative over the requested native
adjacency, not merely absence of positive rows on an unfinished page.

| Situation | Required result and continuation |
| --- | --- |
| Complete nonempty map | `resolved`; exact union count; stop for a direct question or continue the actual workflow |
| Present in the selected layers but no neighbors in the requested direction | `resolved`; empty map and measured zero; layer-absence lists empty |
| Multiplex member absent from some or all selected layers | `resolved`; absent layers contribute no adjacency and are named explicitly; an all-absent scope can complete with zero |
| Query outside the multiplex | `not_found/defer`; `missing_gene_ids` identifies it; `layer_results`, `neighbors`, both total-count locations, `layers_without_gene`, and `collection` are unavailable/null; all neighbor checks unchecked |
| Requested first K rows returned with all their scoped support | `resolved`; the bounded request is complete even if the full collection is not |
| A required tool call fails without recovery | `error/defer`; use the attributed failure shape and preserve supported partials |

In the not-found branch there is no nested `collection.total_count` field because
`collection` itself is null. Preserve the membership evidence; do not claim a
confirmed zero or a completed neighbor lookup.

## Reuse context, finish retrieval, and preserve partial work

<a id="s24-evidence"></a>
A no-call answer needs the right gene, graph version, scope, direction, and
selection. A saved complete map can answer that same complete request. It can
also be projected to a narrower scope: remove other supports, drop rows with no
remaining support, recompute counts, then apply any requested canonical-ID
prefix. Retain the evidence used for that calculation. A saved bounded map can
answer the same bounded request or a shorter prefix in the same scope; it
cannot generally be projected to a different scope or extended to a longer
prefix. An omitted neighbor is not a checked negative.

Complete S2.3 lists can also supply the map. An incident request needs one
undirected list per undirected layer and both directional lists per directed
layer. Reuse the sufficient pieces, retrieve only what is missing, and regroup
by neighbor ID. Deduplicate identical edges, neighbor rows, and evidence; reject
conflicting reuse of an edge or evidence ID. Evidence of layer absence can
supply both empty directed sides without redundant calls. Incoming-only
context cannot stand in for outgoing adjacency.

For a regrouped complete result, the model calculates the unique-neighbor count
from the union of the visible complete lists. For a single map response, it
copies the supplied count. A total hidden in a construction oracle is not
visible runtime evidence. Unknown totals stay null unless an exhaustive
complete traversal supports calculating them. Check supplied totals for
agreement with that accumulation.

Pagination follows S2.3. Start at `cursor:null`; copy a returned cursor exactly
and keep the gene, scope, direction, mode, K, and graph version fixed. Each
page has complete support for its own neighbor rows. Accumulate from the first
page through exhaustion before answering a complete request. Retain every
supporting page record, deduplicate identical rows, and reject inconsistent
support or totals. A last page with `next_cursor:null` can still be incomplete
by itself. A null cursor in top-K mode ends only the bounded traversal. Changing
selection starts a new traversal at null; never invent or repurpose a cursor.

Failures retain the shared fixed result:

```text
result: {
  failed_tool: string,
  error_code: string,
  arguments: exact failed tool arguments,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: LayerMapCoverage | NeighborCollectionCoverage | null
}
```

`LayerMapCoverage` is the ordinary coverage shape above, appropriate to saved
map observations and map pages. If a later page fails, all layers may already
have been evaluated while further neighbor rows remain unavailable. The saved
page metadata and blocker must make that unfinished retrieval explicit.

When assembling a map from separately complete native lists, use the finer
coverage below. It identifies the missing direction rather than hiding it in
an apparently complete layer. Here “checked” means that native collection has
been completely retrieved or established empty by valid membership evidence.
This is a different operation from map-selection coverage; do not interchange
the two meanings.

```text
NeighborCollectionCoverage: {
  operation: neighbor_collections,
  requested_inputs: [{layer_id: string, direction: in | out | undirected}, ...],
  checked_inputs: [{layer_id: string, direction: in | out | undirected}, ...],
  unchecked_inputs: [{layer_id: string, direction: in | out | undirected}, ...]
}
```

Order native inputs by manifest layer, then incoming before outgoing. Checked
and unchecked inputs form an exact disjoint partition. A partially retrieved
native list remains unchecked, while its successful pages remain in
`partial_results`. Do not attach full-scope supporting-layer counts to an
ordinary partial map: retain the original observations and their actual scopes.
If no graph scope has been established, failure coverage is null.

The worked outages are explicitly injected harness scenarios. A failed call
adds no graph evidence. Retry only when the visible runtime allowance permits
it; these examples supply that allowance as `retries_remaining` in the tool
error message. Use the identical failed tool and arguments, including any cursor. Stop
retrying immediately after recovery, then finish any remaining work. Exhaustion
requires backend recovery, not automatically a new user answer.

## Diagnostics and limits on interpretation

<a id="s24-diagnostics"></a>
Keep the approved identity, ambiguity, invalid-input, and scope protocols.
Do not call the graph with unresolved candidates. The family diagnostic retains
the original request, including raw gene text:

```text
result: {
  issue_code: string,
  request: {
    gene: string,
    multiplex_id: string | null,
    layer_scope: LayerScope | null,
    direction: incident | in | out | undirected | null,
    mode: complete | top_k | null,
    top_k: integer | null,
    cursor: string | null,
    ranking: strongest_unspecified | null
  },
  rejected_arguments: exact seven-field MapArguments | null,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...]
}
```

The diagnostic's selection records what the user requested; it is not itself a
call. `ranking:strongest_unspecified` records an unresolved strongest-neighbor
request. A known representation mismatch uses
`invalid_input/DIRECTION_UNAVAILABLE`; missing K uses
`invalid_input/MISSING_LIMIT`; invalid selection or cursor uses
`invalid_input/INVALID_SELECTION` or `invalid_input/INVALID_CURSOR`.
Unspecified cross-layer ranking uses `ambiguous/NEIGHBOR_RANKING_AMBIGUOUS`.
Explain the real missing prerequisite. A local rejection has
`rejected_arguments:null` and needs no graph call. A tool rejection uses the
shared empty-provenance `{issue_code, arguments}` result; copy those exact
arguments into the final diagnostic without inventing a supported partial.

Ordinary answers omit claim cards. When explicit claim calibration is requested,
use the approved `supported_claims`/`unsupported_claims` names and meanings.
This map supports recorded direct adjacency, direction where retained, and
the scoped layer supports shown. TF direction can support recorded regulator
and target roles under the approved source rules. It does not establish
activation, repression, causality, or the sign of regulation from a positive
weight. Coexpression is not physical binding. Reciprocal edges are not by
themselves a feedback mechanism. Several layer supports do not automatically
mean independent confirmations or a stronger comparable score. A checked lack
of direct neighbors in one direction/scope says nothing about longer paths or
other contexts. Identical scoped evidence must license the same claims here
as in S1 and the already reviewed S2 families.

## Real source facts and count-range sampling

<a id="s24-sources"></a>
These examples use the unchanged four complete source files and version in the
[source catalogue](#shared-fixture), with the same 19,033-node multiplex union.
They are not an induced graph on the few illustrated genes. New query identities
MFRP, C1QTNF5, and HNF1A match the pinned index and original Ensembl 116 GTF
(gene-record lines 6,341,831; 6,543,586; and 7,365,047 respectively).

| Query and scope | Verified facts |
| --- | --- |
| MFRP (`ENSG00000235718`), PPI + coexpression | One unique neighbor, C1QTNF5 (`ENSG00000223953`); PPI weight 0.457457457457457 at line 994199 and coexpression weight 0.445400228722821 at line 21809 |
| C1QTNF5, PPI + coexpression | PPI has ENSG00000104969 at 0.56649078845673 (line 359158), ENSG00000197860 at 0.598336305944239 (line 987888), and MFRP above; coexpression has only MFRP; union count three |
| C1QTNF5, both TF layers | Absent from both selected layers, but present in the multiplex; checked empty map |
| DEFB124, PPI + brain TF | Two PPI neighbors from S2.3; absent brain TF |
| CDC27, coexpression + CD4 | Coexpression neighbors ENSG00000153140 at 0.385928536625312 (line 52877), ENSG00000187266 at 0.401670986614128 (line 35445), ENSG00000197465 at 0.387697140897874 (line 47204); CD4 has CREBBP → CDC27 at 1 (line 2426), no outgoing edge; union count four |

The source catalogue is reviewer information, not automatic model context.
Worked reasoning names a gene symbol only when the user or visible identity
context supplies it. Responses below model a future runtime over these real
records. Pagination boundaries, fault injection, and the deliberately
incompatible metadata in .24 are harness scenarios, not observed backend events
or claims about an actual older graph.

<a id="s24-sampling"></a>
Carry forward the approved [range-sampling policy](#s22-sampling). Do not freeze
S2.4 at two selected layers just because that makes a compact review example.
For each eligible view, sample subset sizes from one through its actual eligible
layer count, then vary layer identities and combinations. Preserve all-layer and
all-family requests as exhaustive scopes. For directed-only requests, the
eligible range contains only the directed representations; an explicitly mixed
incompatible request remains a separate diagnostic case.

Within those scope/direction strata, sample attainable unique-neighbor counts
and supporting-layer counts from the real data. Also vary overlap, membership
patterns, reciprocal edges, and the requested K relative to the actual union
size. Use below/equal/above-total K contrasts where possible. Give attainable
count strata equal weight by default before sampling records within them;
report any conditioning or budget-driven departures. Do not invent graph facts
to fill an unattainable integer or change content when the wording bank grows.

The complete four-file incident audit finds **916 attainable positive unique-
neighbor counts, spanning 1–2,975** among the 19,033 multiplex members. This is
a set of observed counts, not every integer in that interval. Zero is absent
from this full-view member stratum but is real for selected subsets and
directions, as the worked cases show. Across all query–neighbor relations, the
observed supporting-layer counts are 1, 2, and 3; 4 is unattainable in this view.
Their counts are respectively 2,514,305; 26,174; and 106. These are source-audit
statistics for corpus construction, not values the model may infer from a
short result. Five retained self-loops account for the odd relation total.

Recompute these domains for the actual production view, split, and candidate
policy. This four-layer review view does not cap production layer counts. Pin
sources, seed, eligible ranges, and sampling histograms; audit wording/outcome
independence. Preserve frozen evaluation panels. Large unions require a real
context/token-budget strategy and complete page traversal where requested;
do not silently remove high-count strata or relabel truncated answers complete.

<a id="s24-decisions"></a>
Revision `S2.4-r1`, 2026-10-26, is **approved**. The user accepted all S2.4
changes and requested that they be recorded in the document. Approval is
recorded at `S2-design-r9`. R10 reopened only M2’s empty-family clause to match
S2.2; the user approved that alignment alongside S2.5 at `S2-design-r11`,
2026-10-27. All other reviewed semantics and every worked trace are retained.

| Decision | State | Approved behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 — one row per neighbor | approved (2026-10-26) | Preserve every supporting layer and native edge; deduplicate union rows and count each supporting layer once |
| M2 — native direction and membership | approved, including alignment (2026-10-27) | Retain native direction and membership distinctions; valid empty-family selection follows S2.2, as approved in [S2.5 L6](#s25-empty-family-alignment) |
| M3 — selection and completeness | approved (2026-10-26) | Complete versus canonical-ID first-K maps; every returned row has full scoped support; no implicit cross-layer strongest ranking |
| M4 — context, partials, and retrieval | approved (2026-10-26) | Reuse sufficient complete lists/maps; follow selection-bound cursors; distinguish map-selection coverage from missing native collections; preserve partials and permitted retries |
| M5 — real examples and sampling | approved (2026-10-26) | Retain eight original roles, add seventeen contrasts, and apply full attainable scope/count sampling without a two-layer training ceiling |
