# S2.5: Gene Layer Membership

<a id="s25-review"></a>
> **Review state: approved**, revision `S2.5-r1`; human approval recorded in
> `S2-design-r11`, 2026-10-27. Approval includes the editorial follow-up and
> S2.4's empty-family alignment. All 25 worked traces are retained.
> These are design-document changes, not deployed tools or published corpora.

## What this family should teach

Answer **which layers contain this gene**, using the requested view and scope.
Keep three facts separate: registry identity, membership in the multiplex, and
membership in each selected layer. A valid identity need not occur in the graph.
A multiplex member need not occur in every family or layer.

The main correction is to original case .6. When membership itself is the
question, a checked absence is a successful answer: `resolved`, `present:false`,
an empty layer list, and count zero. This restores the reviewed S1 membership
convention and the [shared requested-operation rule](#shared-specification).
It does not change edge or neighbor prerequisites: an absent multiplex endpoint
still leaves those operations unavailable. Do not ask for another gene merely
because the answer to a membership question is negative.

The [S0/S1 lessons](#what-we-learned-from-s0-and-s1) call for explicit reasoning
about the outer request. Listing no containing layers can finish a direct
question or supply a useful result for a workflow step. If the outer task also
requires an operation that cannot proceed without graph membership, completing
the classification alone does not complete that larger task. Continue, stop,
or defer based on what the actual request still needs.

## Membership comes from the declared node sets

<a id="s25-membership"></a>
Replace the old blanket statement that a gene is a node exactly when it has an
edge. The authoritative node inventory defines membership. A layer can retain
isolated nodes; an induced subgraph can also omit a member's external neighbors.
Neither case makes the gene absent from the full layer.

For this particular source view, each layer's node set is the union of both
endpoint columns of its complete source file, and the multiplex node set is the
union of those four layer sets. There is no separate isolated-node inventory.
This is a pinned construction rule for these examples, not a universal graph
definition. Every layer node must belong to the declared multiplex node set.
A future view with a separate multiplex inventory may therefore have a
multiplex member that appears in no layer; do not infer global absence merely
from an empty all-layer list.

Membership has no incoming/outgoing selector. For example, CDC27 belongs to both
TF layers even though it has zero outgoing neighbors in each. A target-only
node is still a node. Direction remains part of edge and neighbor observations,
but neither zero outgoing degree nor zero incoming degree establishes absence.
An authoritative neighbor result can establish membership through its explicit
membership fields, as illustrated in [case .19](#s25-19).

## Scope, family, and selection

<a id="s25-scope"></a>
Use the approved typed `layer_scope`: `all` with no family selects every
registered layer; `all` with a family selects that family's registered layers;
`layers` selects an explicit subset. Normalize an explicit list by removing
duplicates and ordering it by the manifest. A completed subset answer does not
enumerate membership outside that subset.

Keep S1's six family values: `ppi`, `coexpression`, `tf_target`, `bulk_pen`,
`scpen`, and `other`. Use the reviewed family mapping, not a loose tag-prefix
guess. In particular, the HumanNet prefix alone does not identify PPI. Valid
layer grammar does not establish that a layer is registered in this view.

**A valid family can select no registered layers.** Under the S2.2 rule, this is
an empty selection, not an unknown family. The answer can be a computed empty
list with count zero and empty requested/checked/unchecked layer lists. Report
that the view contains no layer of that family; do not recast this as gene
absence from actual layers or as biological non-expression. A separate unknown
family token or unregistered layer remains a diagnostic.

<a id="s25-empty-family-alignment"></a>
**Alignment approved on 2026-10-27:** S2.2 already permits this valid
empty selection, while S2.4 mistakenly required a scope diagnostic. The S2.4
sentence now follows S2.2: after its own membership
prerequisite is satisfied, an empty selected family yields a resolved empty
neighbor map. Only that part of S2.4 decision M2 was amended; its other approved
rules and all 25 worked traces remain unchanged. S2.5 itself can resolve an
empty membership list even when multiplex membership is false, because that
absence answers the requested membership question. [Case .21](#s25-21) shows
the valid-empty-family boundary using the real manifest.

An explicitly empty layer list is different from a valid family that expands
to zero layers: keep the existing `invalid_input/INVALID_SELECTION` rule for
the empty explicit list. Do not silently default a missing scope to a layer
from its position in context.

## Proposed call and result

<a id="s25-interface"></a>
Resolve identities with S1 normalization and candidate handling. Preserve raw
registry lookup inputs and exact returned IDs. A supplied authoritative identity
record avoids a redundant lookup; a canonical ID can be passed directly to the
membership tool. Its graph result is not proof of registry resolution. Do not
pass unresolved symbol candidates to this single-gene operation.

All six arguments are explicit:

```text
get_gene_layers({
  multiplex_id: string,
  gene_id: canonical gene ID,
  layer_scope: LayerScope,
  mode: complete | top_k,
  top_k: positive integer | null,
  cursor: string | null
})
```

`complete` asks for all containing layers and requires `top_k:null`. `top_k`
asks for the first K containing layers in manifest order, using the S2.2
ordering convention. This is not a ranking by degree, weight, importance, or
biological relevance. Require a positive explicit K. Omitting the bound must
not mean both “all” and “apply a default limit.” Start a traversal at null.

A successful tool response contains `{status:"resolved", provenance, result}`.
The ordinary final answer uses the same fixed result shape:

```text
result: {
  gene_id: canonical gene ID,
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_scope: LayerScope,
  present: boolean,
  layer_ids: [containing layer ID, ...],
  layer_count: nonnegative integer | null,
  coverage: {
    operation: layer_membership,
    requested_layer_ids: [layer ID, ...],
    checked_layer_ids: [layer ID, ...],
    unchecked_layer_ids: [layer ID, ...]
  },
  collection: {
    mode: complete | top_k,
    returned_count: nonnegative integer,
    total_count: nonnegative integer | null,
    complete: boolean,
    next_cursor: string | null
  }
}
```

`present` retains S1's meaning: **membership in the multiplex**, even when the
selected scope is one layer or a family with no layers. The tool classifies
that global membership from the authoritative multiplex inventory as part of
the acquisition. It must not compute `present:false` from a negative family
list. No separate model call is required when the tool already provides this
fact. Scope metadata identifies the requested layer operation; the explicit
`present` field carries the multiplex-membership observation.

`layer_ids` contains the returned positive memberships, in manifest order.
`layer_count` and `collection.total_count` refer to the full positive count in
the **selected scope**, not necessarily the whole multiplex. They must agree,
including when both are unknown/null. `returned_count` is the length of the
returned list. Remove duplicate layers when combining observations; never sum
overlapping scoped counts. A complete list has a known exact count equal to
its length. A bounded request can finish with an incomplete collection.

Coverage records evaluation of the requested layer selection. A resolved page
or bounded response may mark all selected layers checked while withholding
some positive layer IDs. **An omitted layer is not a checked negative merely
because coverage says “checked.”** Negatives require an exhaustive compatible
list or another explicit membership observation. The collection metadata
separately states whether the returned list is exhaustive. For a successful
empty family selection, all three coverage lists are empty.

| Observation | Ordinary membership answer |
| --- | --- |
| Gene appears in selected layers | `resolved`, `present:true`, returned containing layers and scoped count |
| Gene is a multiplex member but absent from every selected layer | `resolved`, `present:true`, complete empty list and count zero |
| Gene is confirmed outside the multiplex | `resolved`, `present:false`, complete empty list and count zero; every selected layer is checked negative by containment |
| Valid family has no registered layers | `resolved`, empty selection and count zero; `present` still reports the independently supported multiplex fact |
| Identity/scope is unresolved or a required backend lookup is unavailable | Diagnostic/failure branch; do not fabricate an ordinary empty membership answer |

The old `missing_gene_ids` field is unnecessary for this single-gene membership
classification; `present` states the observed positive or negative directly.
The old optional `layer_family` argument becomes the typed scope. These new
graph shapes require a future shared contract version and new source-derived
corpora. They do not rewrite S1's published outputs or its frozen evaluation
keys. The corrected resolved-negative status itself agrees with reviewed S1.

## Reuse evidence and preserve incomplete work

<a id="s25-evidence"></a>
A saved complete record can answer the same question without a call. It can
also be filtered to a covered family or subset using the visible manifest,
with counts recomputed for that requested scope. Keep the original evidence
record and scope; do not relabel the acquisition as if it had been a new call.
A complete family record cannot enumerate memberships in other families.
Reuse it and evaluate only the still-unchecked layers, as in [case .7](#s25-7).

When combining complete scoped results, require matching gene, multiplex,
version, and global `present` value. Their checked scopes must cover every
requested layer. Merge unique positive IDs in manifest order and calculate
the union count from the visible data. Conflicting membership or evidence-ID
reuse prevents a valid aggregate; retain the records and report the conflict
rather than choosing a convenient answer. Deduplicate identical evidence.

A saved bounded result can answer the same bounded request or a shorter prefix
within the same scope. It cannot generally answer a complete request or be
filtered to a different scope: previously unseen layers may belong in that
result. A known total does not reveal the omitted identities. Request the
missing information rather than filling it from the source catalogue.

Global membership also needs visible support in a no-call answer. It may come
from an explicit multiplex check, the `present` field, or an authoritative
positive layer membership, since every layer node is a multiplex node.
A negative filtered list alone never proves global absence. Confirmed global
absence, however, proves absence from every layer in the same version and can
finish this membership question without per-layer calls, as in [case .20](#s25-20).
An induced-subgraph omission does not supply either full-layer or global absence.

Pagination follows S2.3/S2.4. Copy each returned cursor unchanged and keep the
gene, scope, mode, K, and graph version fixed. A complete request needs all pages
from the initial cursor through exhaustion. Preserve every supporting page,
deduplicate identical layer IDs, and reject inconsistent membership or totals.
The last page can have `complete:false` by itself; only the accumulated list is
complete. A null cursor in top-K mode ends the bounded traversal, not necessarily
the full list. Changing selection starts a new traversal at null.

Copy counts supplied by the tool. For a regrouped result, explicitly calculate
the count from the visible complete union. If a tool omits the full total, leave
it null unless exhaustive retrieval supports counting the entire collection.
The construction oracle is not runtime evidence.

An unrecovered required failure uses the shared fixed shape:

```text
result: {
  failed_tool: string,
  error_code: string,
  arguments: exact failed arguments,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: LayerMembershipCoverage | null
}
```

`LayerMembershipCoverage` uses the same requested/checked/unchecked layer
fields as above, for the outer requested scope. Independently completed scopes
remain checked; failed unevaluated scopes remain unchecked. For a failed later
page, earlier selection evaluation may already cover every layer even though
the remaining positive IDs are unavailable. Preserve the original page metadata
and name the missing page as the blocker. Coverage alone never turns a partial
list into an exhaustive answer. Use null coverage when no graph scope has been
established. A failed call contributes no new evidence.

The worked outages are injected harness scenarios. Their tool-error messages
supply the runtime allowance as `retries_remaining`. Retry only within that
allowance, repeating the identical tool and arguments, including the cursor.
Stop retrying after recovery, then finish any remaining task. Exhaustion needs
backend recovery; do not automatically ask the user for a different gene.

## Diagnostics and claim limits

<a id="s25-diagnostics"></a>
Use this fixed diagnostic branch when a prerequisite cannot be resolved:

```text
result: {
  issue_code: string,
  request: {
    gene: string,
    multiplex_id: string | null,
    layer_scope: LayerScope | null,
    mode: complete | top_k | null,
    top_k: integer | null,
    cursor: string | null
  },
  rejected_arguments: exact six-field MembershipArguments | null,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...]
}
```

Keep original gene text and valid identity/candidate partials. Unresolved
identity uses the approved S1 status meanings; a confirmed registry lookup
failure is not the same as a resolved graph-membership negative. Missing scope
is `invalid_input/MISSING_SCOPE`; an unknown registered multiplex or layer is
`not_found/UNKNOWN_MULTIPLEX` or `not_found/UNKNOWN_LAYER`. An unsupported family
value is `invalid_input/INVALID_LAYER_FAMILY`; preserve the requested string
in the diagnostic scope, even though it is not a valid tool selector. An empty
explicit list or invalid mode/K combination uses
`invalid_input/INVALID_SELECTION`; missing K uses `invalid_input/MISSING_LIMIT`;
an invalid/stale cursor uses `invalid_input/INVALID_CURSOR`.

A known local rejection needs no tool call and sets `rejected_arguments:null`.
A tool rejection returns the shared empty-provenance `{issue_code, arguments}`
result; preserve its exact six arguments in `rejected_arguments`. Retain any
usable earlier observations as attributed partials, but do not fabricate
evidence for the rejection itself. A syntactically valid, unregistered layer
must not be turned into a measured negative, as [case .22](#s25-22) shows.

Ordinary answers omit claim cards. Explicit calibration uses the approved
`supported_claims`/`unsupported_claims` names and canonical vocabulary, with
the same subjects, version, and scope limits as other families:

- Known multiplex membership plus checked absence from an actual layer
  supports `gene_not_node_in_layer` and the shared scoped edge/path absence
  claims for that endpoint. A different family label does not remove those
  permissions from identical evidence.
- Confirmed multiplex absence supports `gene_not_node_in_multiplex`. Edge and
  path operations still have their own unavailable-prerequisite behavior;
  do not report that those searches ran and returned negatives. Deriving an
  empty membership list does not silently extend claim-card permissions.
- An omitted bounded-list entry is not confirmed layer absence. An empty
  registered-family selection contains no actual layer about which to assert
  gene absence.
- Membership in a TF layer does not identify a regulator or target role.
  Membership in PPI does not establish physical interaction with an arbitrary
  partner. Membership in PEN does not supply expression level, and absence from
  PEN does not establish non-expression. Other contexts and versions require
  their own evidence.

Do not impose the old five-layer summary threshold. Keep prose readable for
the request, and retain the structured list and counts regardless of summary
length. Score structured correctness and evidence, not exact summary wording.

## Real data and attainable count ranges

<a id="s25-sources"></a>
Use the unchanged [four-file source view](#shared-fixture) and graph version.
All memberships and absences below were checked against complete endpoint
inventories. These identities were already verified in earlier family reviews;
no invented graph fixtures or new gene identities are needed.

| Query | Complete containing layers in manifest order |
| --- | --- |
| SLC4A11 (`ENSG00000088836`) | HumanNetV3:string_ppi |
| C1QTNF5 (`ENSG00000223953`) | HumanNetV3:string_ppi; HumanNetV3:coexpression |
| MFRP (`ENSG00000235718`) | HumanNetV3:string_ppi; HumanNetV3:coexpression; TFs:brain |
| CDC27 (`ENSG00000004897`) | All four layers, including TFs:cd4+t_cells |
| NFYA (`ENSG00000001167`) | HumanNetV3:string_ppi; TFs:brain |
| CCT8L1P (`ENSG00000020219`) | None; confirmed outside the multiplex |

CDC27 has zero outgoing neighbors in both TF layers but nine incoming brain
neighbors and one incoming CD4 neighbor. Its layer membership is therefore a
real direction-sensitive contrast to an incorrect outgoing-degree shortcut.
The view registers no `bulk_pen`, `scpen`, or `other` layer. Empty selections
for those valid families must not stand in for gene-absence examples in actual
PEN/other layers. Those need a future expanded, pinned view with real records.

The reviewer can inspect the source catalogue; the model receives only the
listed harness metadata and each trace's visible observations. Wrong-version
context in .23 is an explicitly injected metadata incompatibility, not a claim
about a real historical snapshot. Page boundaries and backend failures are
also harness scenarios over the verified source facts.

<a id="s25-sampling"></a>
Apply the approved [range-sampling policy](#s22-sampling). Remove fixed numeric
roles such as “six layers” or “four layers”: sample actual attainable membership
counts across the chosen view and candidate policy. Vary explicit subset sizes
from one through the eligible layer count, and vary the identities of those
layers. All-layer and all-family requests remain exhaustive selections.

The fresh audit of all 19,033 multiplex nodes gives:

| Number of containing layers in the full four-layer view | Multiplex nodes |
| ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3,525 |
| 2 | 5,703 |
| 3 | 7,112 |
| 4 | 2,693 |

For the two-layer TF family, the counts among those same multiplex members are
zero layers: **5,503**; one layer: **9,881**; two layers: **3,649**. Every one of
the 15 nonempty explicit layer subsets was also audited. Use its actual count
domain rather than assuming all integers are attainable for a particular
conditioned candidate set.

Candidate policy matters. Of the graph's 19,033 nodes, 18,851 occur in the pinned
Ensembl index; the other 182 remain graph nodes in this unfiltered source view.
Do not silently remove them from its membership definition. Among registered
IDs, 60,090 are outside this view and supply real zero-membership candidates.
Keep registry-conditioned sampling histograms separate from whole-graph
histograms. The registry is identity evidence, not a replacement graph inventory.

Sample attainable count strata equally by default, then real examples within
them; report conditioning or budget departures. Vary overlap, membership
patterns, family, subset size, and K below/equal/above the observed positive
count. Separate zeros caused by a selected-scope absence, global absence, and
a family with no registered layers. Do not invent an isolated node to fill a
stratum unavailable in these files. The four-layer review view is not a
production limit: broader production scopes require their own pins and audits.

Keep content choices independent of the wording bank; pin sources, seeds, and
histograms. Preserve frozen evaluation panels and current-turn reasoning.
Use actual tokenizer/context-budget checks for long layer lists and complete
traversals rather than silently dropping large-count cases or adding caps.

# S2.6: Nodes by Layer

<a id="s26-review"></a>
> **Review state: approved**, revision `S2.6-r1`; human approval recorded
> in `S2-design-r12`, 2026-10-27. The user accepted N1–N6 and directed the
> review to S2.7. All 25 worked traces are retained. These are design-document
> changes, not deployed tools, published corpora, or evaluation keys.

## What this family should teach

Given a finite list of genes and **one registered layer**, classify every
requested gene. S2.5 asks which layers contain one gene; S2.6 asks which of the
supplied genes belong to one layer. Neither question asks for neighbors or for
an inventory of every gene in the layer.

Keep three disjoint groups:

| Group | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `layer_gene_ids` | Requested genes that belong to the selected layer |
| `not_in_layer_gene_ids` | Requested genes that belong to the multiplex but not to this layer |
| `missing_gene_ids` | Requested genes confirmed absent from the multiplex |

A gene in the last group is a completed membership negative. It is not an
unchecked input or a failed identity lookup. All three groups together resolve
the classification, even when the positive group is empty. An unresolved
identity, an unknown layer, or a required backend failure needs its own branch.
The old statement that every answer is resolved applies only to a completed
classification, not to these blocked requests.

A direct question stops after this partition is known. A classification requested
as a step in a larger workflow can continue with a negative result. If the outer
request additionally requires an operation whose prerequisites are absent, that
operation still needs its own status and blocker; the classification alone does
not complete the compound request.

## Input, node membership, and ordering

<a id="s26-inputs"></a>
Use the same [authoritative node-set rule](#s25-membership) as S2.5. A layer member
is also a multiplex member. Layer membership does not depend on positive incoming
or outgoing degree. A target-only directed node belongs to the layer. An induced
subgraph's omitted neighbors do not show absence from the full layer.

For this [four-file view](#shared-fixture), node inventories are the unions of
both endpoint columns, and the multiplex inventory is their union. Future views
may include explicit isolated nodes. Do not fabricate such an inventory for this
view or silently discard graph nodes absent from the registry index.

The task must select one registered layer. Valid layer syntax alone is not
registration. This family does not accept an all-family selector; a valid family
with zero layers is not a substitute for the required single layer. Keep all six
S1 family meanings and the approved native layer strings.

Resolve symbols using the exact S1 identity rules. Preserve raw lookup inputs
and returned canonical IDs, candidates, and null symbols. An authoritative
registry record can avoid a duplicate lookup. Canonical IDs may be passed directly
to the graph tool; graph membership does not prove registry validity. Do not
silently replace unresolved symbols with guessed IDs or expand one ambiguous
symbol into several requested genes. Keep unresolved inputs and completed mappings
in the diagnostic branch until the requested identities are settled.

After identity resolution, remove duplicate canonical IDs in first-mention order.
Use this order in `gene_ids` and all three coverage lists. Each result category
is instead sorted by ascending canonical ID and contains no duplicates. Two
input symbols that resolve to the same ID request one membership classification.
The original input spellings remain available in the request and any registry
observations; do not rewrite raw registry arguments.

## Complete-batch call and result

<a id="s26-interface"></a>
All three arguments are required:

```text
get_nodes_by_layer({
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: string,
  gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...]
})
```

This operation classifies **every supplied ID**. It has no direction selector,
implicit top-K limit, or cursor. Successful responses are atomic for that batch:
all inputs are classified, or the response uses a diagnostic/failure branch.
The explicit finite input list defines the requested extent. A user asking for
every node in a layer has requested a different operation and must not receive
only a silently chosen input subset.

Large requests may use several complete batches only when an explicit runtime
batch constraint or the actual context budget requires it. Preserve first-mention
order when dividing the unique input list. Accumulate all three categories,
retain every batch's evidence, and compute the final counts over their unique
union. A failed batch leaves those inputs unchecked; never return a successful
answer after silently dropping a batch. Do not invent a fixed size cap for this
document or add a paging convention that the tool does not expose.

A successful tool response contains `{status:"resolved", provenance, result}`.
The ordinary final result has this fixed shape:

```text
result: {
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: string,
  layer_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  layer_gene_count: nonnegative integer,
  not_in_layer_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  missing_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  coverage: {
    operation: layer_membership,
    requested_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
    checked_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
    unchecked_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...]
  },
  collection: {
    mode: complete,
    returned_count: nonnegative integer,
    total_count: nonnegative integer,
    complete: true,
    next_cursor: null
  }
}
```

For a successful answer, the three categories form an exact disjoint partition
of `coverage.requested_gene_ids`. `checked_gene_ids` equals the requested list
in the same order and `unchecked_gene_ids` is empty. An input confirmed outside
the multiplex is checked and belongs only to `missing_gene_ids`; do not also
place it in `not_in_layer_gene_ids`.

`layer_gene_count`, `collection.returned_count`, and `collection.total_count`
all equal the length of `layer_gene_ids`. These are counts of positive matches
**among the requested genes**, not the total number of nodes in the layer. The
collection describes that positive list; coverage describes classification of
all inputs. The negative categories are exhaustive too. Copy tool counts when
copying one answer; explicitly calculate counts after filtering or combining
visible complete classifications.

An explicitly supplied empty gene list is a valid empty classification once the
multiplex and layer are known. It needs no graph call, has empty categories and
coverage, count zero, and empty provenance. This is set classification over an
empty domain; it asserts nothing about the layer's overall size. A missing or
null gene list is different and uses `invalid_input/MISSING_GENES`. These rules
also distinguish an explicit empty list from a required list whose identities
have not been resolved.

## Evidence reuse, partial answers, and failures

<a id="s26-evidence"></a>
Use visible authoritative evidence for the same IDs, multiplex, graph version,
and layer. A larger complete classification can be restricted to the requested
subset. Recompute counts and coverage for that subset while preserving the
original evidence acquisition, scope, and ID. Records need not have the same
input order; the new answer's coverage follows the current request.

A compatible multiplex-membership **positive** does not decide layer membership.
A compatible multiplex-membership **negative** does: it puts that gene in
`missing_gene_ids` without a layer call. When supplied context contains both,
query only the genes whose layer classification remains unknown. The old blanket
instruction to always call after a multiplex record is therefore narrowed to
unresolved layer classifications.

A complete S2.5 containing-layer list can establish membership or absence in a
covered layer, with its explicit global `present` value separating the two
negative categories. A returned positive in a bounded S2.5 list is usable, but
omission from an incomplete list is not a negative. Its checked-layer coverage
alone does not reveal the omitted membership result. A resolved neighbor record
with both membership-absence lists empty establishes the query's membership,
even when its outgoing neighbor list is empty.

For partial context, retain established categories and fetch only the remaining
IDs. Combine compatible observations by gene, with no double counting. The same
gene cannot occupy conflicting categories. A conflicting record or evidence ID
must be surfaced as a harness/data fault; do not choose the convenient category.
An old-version record cannot fill a current-version gap. Deduplicate identical
evidence and keep the supporting records in first-use order.

Use the shared failure shape for an unrecovered required lookup:

```text
result: {
  failed_tool: string,
  error_code: string,
  arguments: exact failed call arguments,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: GeneMembershipCoverage | null
}
```

`GeneMembershipCoverage` has the same four fields shown above, referring to the
outer requested genes and one selected layer. Independently known positive and
negative classifications are checked. Failed attempted inputs stay unchecked.
Use null coverage when a valid common graph scope or canonical input domain has
not been established. Keep each successful earlier observation in its complete
attributed partial-result shape, including registry mappings when they were used.
Do not synthesize an ordinary incomplete partition with empty placeholders for
unknown categories. Failed calls add no evidence.

The worked errors are explicit fault-injection scenarios. Retry only when the
error response permits another attempt through `retries_remaining`. Repeat the
identical tool and arguments, stop retrying after recovery, and defer after a
terminal or exhausted failure. A checked membership negative never permits a
retry. Name backend recovery as the blocker when the backend is unavailable.

## Diagnostics and claim limits

<a id="s26-diagnostics"></a>
Use this fixed diagnostic result for an unresolved prerequisite:

```text
result: {
  issue_code: string,
  request: {
    genes: original supplied JSON value | null,
    multiplex_id: string | null,
    layer_id: string | null
  },
  rejected_arguments: exact three-field NodesByLayerArguments | null,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...]
}
```

Preserve the literal supplied JSON value in `request.genes`, including an
invalid scalar or invalid list. For a supplied gene list, preserve raw input
order and duplicates; use null when the list is missing. Missing scope uses
`invalid_input/MISSING_SCOPE`; missing genes use `invalid_input/MISSING_GENES`.
An unregistered multiplex or layer uses `not_found/UNKNOWN_MULTIPLEX` or
`not_found/UNKNOWN_LAYER`. Invalid input shape uses
`invalid_input/INVALID_GENE_LIST`. Unresolved identities retain S1 status
meanings: invalid, not-found, and ambiguous identities are not graph negatives.
Keep the original registry result as a partial so that its exact candidates or
invalid input remain visible. The issue code must identify the unresolved
prerequisite. Use `UNRESOLVED_IDENTITY` for an unresolved registry identity;
it must not claim that graph membership was measured.

A known local rejection needs no tool call and uses `rejected_arguments:null`.
A tool rejection carries `{issue_code, arguments}` with empty provenance;
preserve the exact three arguments in `rejected_arguments`. A required registry
backend failure uses the failure branch, not a graph-negative category. In every
blocked branch, retain supported earlier work and give a nonempty blocker.

Ordinary membership answers omit claim cards. Explicit calibration uses only
the shared `supported_claims`/`unsupported_claims` vocabulary and its subject,
scope, version, and prerequisite rules. In particular:

- `not_in_layer_gene_ids` supports `gene_not_node_in_layer` and the approved
  scoped edge/path absence claims for those endpoints, given their known
  multiplex membership. Do not remove those permissions merely because a
  different family label appears.
- `missing_gene_ids` supports `gene_not_node_in_multiplex`. It does not report
  that an edge or path search ran; those operations have separate unavailable
  prerequisites. Do not silently extend claim-card permissions from containment.
- A positive membership does not establish an arbitrary edge, physical
  interaction, TF role, expression level, or causality. Neither negative group
  establishes biological non-expression or absence in another version.
- A gene omitted from a bounded list is not assigned to a negative category
  unless a separate sufficient observation supports that classification.

## Real records and sampling

<a id="s26-sources"></a>
These examples reuse the pinned [four-file source view](#shared-fixture) and
Ensembl 116 identities. The reviewer can inspect the full source catalogue; the
model receives only the common manifest and each trace's visible observations.
Proposed tool results are source-derived expectations, not deployed runtime
transcripts. Wrong-version context and outages are explicitly injected harness
conditions.

| Gene | ID | Layer-membership facts used here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CDC27 | `ENSG00000004897` | Present in all four layers; target-only in both TF layers |
| NFYA | `ENSG00000001167` | Present in PPI and brain TF; absent from coexpression and CD4 TF |
| MFRP | `ENSG00000235718` | Present in PPI, coexpression, and brain TF; absent from CD4 TF |
| C1QTNF5 | `ENSG00000223953` | Present in PPI and coexpression; absent from both TF layers |
| SLC4A11 | `ENSG00000088836` | Present in PPI; absent from the other three layers |
| CCT8L1P | `ENSG00000020219` | Registry-valid; absent from the multiplex |

The complete source inventories contain 19,033 multiplex nodes. Of these,
18,851 occur in the 78,941-ID pinned registry index; 182 graph nodes are outside
that identity index and remain graph nodes. The following populations condition
on registry-valid candidates; the globally absent pool is 60,090 in every row.

| Selected layer | Registered layer members | Registered multiplex members outside layer | Registered IDs outside multiplex |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| HumanNetV3:string_ppi | 17,983 | 868 | 60,090 |
| HumanNetV3:coexpression | 11,857 | 6,994 | 60,090 |
| TFs:brain | 11,313 | 7,538 | 60,090 |
| TFs:cd4+t_cells | 5,687 | 13,164 | 60,090 |

The current view has no registered PEN or `other` layer and no separate isolate
inventory. The original PEN/other example roles are retained using actual PPI,
coexpression, and TF records. Future coverage of those families and full-layer
isolates needs expanded real pinned sources. Empty family selections or zero
outdegree cannot substitute for those missing source cases.

<a id="s26-sampling"></a>
Apply the approved [attainable-range sampling policy](#s22-sampling) to input
set size and all three partition sizes. For each layer and candidate policy,
record the available populations in the layer, elsewhere in the multiplex,
and outside the multiplex. Sample feasible triples of category counts and then
real identities, respecting the distinct-ID budget. Include empty categories,
all-positive and all-negative sets, and singleton and larger requests. Do not
reuse the few numerical sizes in these examples as fixed corpus categories.

Conditioning matters: registry-valid candidates exclude some real graph nodes
from the sampling pool without changing the graph's node definition. Keep whole
node-inventory counts and registry-conditioned counts separate. Sample input
order and duplicates independently of outcomes, vary which identities fill each
category, and pair direct/workflow wordings across matching facts. Content choices
must not depend on the wording-bank size. Use at least 32 reviewed wordings per
framing, preserve frozen held-out rows, and check actual tokenizer/context limits.
Do not silently omit difficult large-input cases or truncate their answers.

# S2.7: Shared Neighbors

<a id="s27-review"></a>
> **Review state: approved**, revision `S2.7-r1`; human approval recorded
> in `S2-design-r13`, 2026-10-27. The user accepted H1–H6 and directed the
> review to S2.8. All 29 worked traces are retained. Runtime implementation
> and corpus construction remain later work.

## What this family should teach

Given two gene roles in one registered layer, compute the exact intersection
of their requested neighbor sets. Keep the acquisition of each set separate
from the final set calculation. One successful lookup does not predict the
other, and two truncated lists do not generally reveal the full intersection.

A completed empty intersection resolves the question. A required lookup that
fails does not produce an empty intersection. Keep supported observations and
defer when the required information remains unavailable. Choose stop or continue
from the user's actual request, including when the answer is negative.

The eight original question roles remain. Their illustrative graph facts and
legacy provenance/claim fields are replaced with the shared conventions and
real source records. In particular, original case .5 now follows the approved
neighbor rule: a known multiplex member absent from the layer has a resolved
empty neighbor set, not an unavailable neighbor operation.

## Queries, direction, and self-loops

<a id="s27-semantics"></a>
Resolve identities and registered scope using the approved S1/S2 rules. Preserve
raw registry inputs and returned IDs, symbols, and candidates. Authoritative
identity context can avoid a lookup; a canonical ID may go directly to the graph
tool. Do not infer a symbol from the reviewer catalogue in model reasoning.

Keep the two query roles in user order, each binding an ID to its direction:

| Requested sets | Meaning of a shared node X |
| --- | --- |
| Undirected neighbors of A and B | A–X and B–X are recorded |
| Outgoing neighbors of A and B | A → X and B → X: a common recorded target |
| Incoming neighbors of A and B | X → A and X → B: a common recorded regulator |
| Outgoing neighbors of A and incoming neighbors of B | A → X and X → B are recorded |
| All incident neighbors of A and B | X lies in each endpoint's union of incoming and outgoing neighbors |

For a directed layer, an unqualified neighbor request means the last row, as
already approved in [S2.3](#s23-both-directions). Use final-only `both` for that
role and acquire incoming then outgoing lists as needed. The primitive tool
directions remain `in`, `out`, and `undirected`. `both` is not a new tool argument.
For an undirected layer, the natural neighbor direction is `undirected`.
Explicit incoming/outgoing roles are unavailable in an undirected representation.

For each role, first form its requested set: one directional list, or the
distinct-ID union of its incoming and outgoing lists. Then intersect the two
role sets. Sort the final shared IDs lexicographically. Do not sort the query
roles away from their directions or interpret an incoming record as outgoing.

The same gene can occupy both roles. Identical gene/direction requests reuse
one acquisition; different directions for that gene remain separate operations.
The intersection of an identical set with itself is that set. Keep both user
roles in `queries`, while deduplicating identical primitive operations in coverage.

Preserve the [S2.3 self-loop rule](#s23-interface). Adjacency alone does not make
either query gene a shared neighbor. A self-loop can put a query gene on its own
list; if it is also on the other requested list, the ordinary set intersection
does include it. Do not silently remove query endpoints. Excluding them would
require an explicit separately defined filter.

## Acquisitions and the fixed computed result

<a id="s27-interface"></a>
Use the unchanged seven-argument neighbor tool:

```text
get_neighbors({
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: string,
  gene_id: canonical gene ID,
  direction: in | out | undirected,
  mode: complete | top_k,
  top_k: positive integer | null,
  cursor: string | null
})
```

New acquisitions for a complete shared-neighbor request use `mode:complete`,
`top_k:null`, and an initial null cursor. Acquire missing primitive queries in
first-role order; expand `both` as incoming then outgoing. Reuse sufficient
compatible context and skip operations whose facts are already known or are
unnecessary to the exact answer. There is no new shared-neighbor backend tool.

Keep the exact S2.3 response shape and neighbor ordering: descending numeric
weight, then ascending ID. Weights support the individual observations, but the
intersection is a set of IDs. Do not average, multiply, rank, or otherwise combine
weights across endpoints or orientations without a requested and defined rule.

The ordinary computed result has this fixed shape:

```text
result: {
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: string,
  queries: [
    {gene_id: canonical gene ID, direction: in | out | undirected | both},
    {gene_id: canonical gene ID, direction: in | out | undirected | both}
  ],
  shared_neighbors: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  shared_neighbor_count: nonnegative integer,
  input_memberships: [
    {gene_id: canonical gene ID,
     present_in_multiplex: true,
     present_in_layer: boolean | null}, ...
  ],
  coverage: {
    operation: neighbor_lists,
    requested_queries: [AtomicNeighborQuery, ...],
    checked_queries: [AtomicNeighborQuery, ...],
    unchecked_queries: [AtomicNeighborQuery, ...]
  },
  collection: {
    mode: complete,
    returned_count: nonnegative integer,
    total_count: nonnegative integer,
    complete: true,
    next_cursor: null
  }
}
```

`AtomicNeighborQuery` has exactly `{gene_id, direction}`, with direction `in`,
`out`, or `undirected`. Expand the two requested roles, remove identical tuples
in first-use order, and retain that order in each coverage list. Every requested
tuple appears in exactly one of checked or unchecked. A tuple is checked only
when its entire neighbor set is known, including a derived empty set after
authoritative layer absence. A partial page or incomplete bounded list alone
does not mark that full-set operation checked.

The final `collection` describes the shared set, not either acquired neighbor
list. Its three counts equal the number of unique `shared_neighbors`. Compute
this count from the visible intersection. A sufficient proof can settle the
entire intersection while leaving one neighbor set unchecked; the next section
defines these cases. Explain that proof instead of pretending the unused set
was retrieved.

`input_memberships` contains each distinct query ID once, in first-mention
order. Both genes must be supported multiplex members for an ordinary answer.
Layer membership is true or false when observed; it can remain null when it is
unneeded for a sufficient intersection proof. Null does not mean layer absence.
This explicit form replaces the legacy final absence arrays. Exact S2.3 arrays
remain unchanged inside tool results and attributed partial observations.

This packet specifies complete shared sets. It has no implicit strongest-K
intersection, hidden list-size cap, or cross-endpoint weight ranking. Explicit
bounded or ranked shared-set requests need their own declared selection rule;
do not substitute the intersection of two strongest-K neighbor lists.

## Sufficient evidence, membership prerequisites, and retrieval

<a id="s27-evidence"></a>
All evidence must match the requested IDs, multiplex, graph version, layer, and
orientation. Preserve original acquisitions and evidence IDs when deriving a
new result; do not relabel their scope or change their data. Keep supporting
evidence in first-use order and deduplicate identical records. Conflicting
weights, membership facts, totals, or evidence-ID reuse are harness/data faults,
not permission to choose a convenient intersection.

| Available evidence | Exact conclusion or remaining work |
| --- | --- |
| Complete sets for both roles | Compute the complete sorted intersection |
| One complete set; the other list missing or insufficient | Obtain the missing information, unless a proof below already settles the result |
| One complete set is wholly included in visible positives of the other | The intersection is exactly that complete set; the other list need not be exhausted |
| One complete role set is empty; both genes are known multiplex members | The intersection is empty, even if the other layer membership/list is unknown |
| Two incomplete lists show common entries | Those entries are a lower bound, not generally the full intersection |
| Incomplete lists show no common entry | The full intersection may still be nonempty |
| A required gene is outside the multiplex | The neighbor predicate is unavailable; do not return an ordinary empty shared set |

The containment proof follows directly from set intersection: if complete A is
contained in observed positive entries of B, then A ∩ B = A. Empty A is its
zero-element case, subject to the same global-membership prerequisites. More
general candidate-by-candidate proofs require explicit compatible evidence for
every candidate; unobserved entries are not negatives. Production examples must
state their proof, rather than learn a rule that two complete calls are always
required.

For `both`, one empty incoming or outgoing set does not make the union empty.
Both orientations must be known empty, or authoritative layer absence must
establish that result. Global absence never becomes a resolved neighbor set,
even when another role has an empty set. A separate authoritative multiplex
record can settle the other gene's global prerequisite without acquiring its
neighbor list; retain that record and leave unobserved layer membership null.

Complete-mode page prefixes can continue using the exact returned cursor and
unchanged selection. Acquire every required page from the initial cursor through
exhaustion, retain its evidence, and deduplicate identical entries. The last page
may be incomplete by itself. Only the accumulated set is complete. Copy non-null
totals and reject conflicting values; if totals were unknown, count an exhausted
complete traversal. A bounded context is a different selection: a new complete
traversal starts at null, not at a cursor invented from the bounded result.
Once a sufficient proof settles the exact intersection, stop acquiring otherwise
unneeded pages and leave any incomplete primitive neighbor set unchecked.

## Failure and diagnostic branches

<a id="s27-diagnostics"></a>
A required unrecovered backend failure uses the shared fixed shape:

```text
result: {
  failed_tool: string,
  error_code: string,
  arguments: exact failed call arguments,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: NeighborQueryCoverage | null
}
```

Coverage uses the same primitive query fields as the ordinary result. A failed
or partially retrieved query remains unchecked, even when identity or membership
is known. Retain all supporting registry records, completed lists, and successful
pages as exact attributed partials. Do not add an empty shared list or zero count
to this branch. Use null coverage before a valid scope and canonical query domain
have been established. Failed calls add no new evidence.

Retry only when the visible runtime error explicitly supplies another attempt
through `retries_remaining`. Repeat the identical tool and arguments; for
`get_neighbors`, this includes all seven fields and the cursor. Stop retrying
after success, finish any remaining required
work, and choose continuation from the outer request. Exhaustion defers for
backend recovery. A checked negative is not a retry allowance.

Use this fixed diagnostic shape for an unresolved prerequisite:

```text
result: {
  issue_code: string,
  request: {
    genes: original supplied JSON value | null,
    multiplex_id: string | null,
    layer_id: string | null,
    directions: original supplied JSON value | null
  },
  rejected_arguments: exact seven-field NeighborArguments | null,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: NeighborQueryCoverage | null
}
```

Keep the raw request order, duplicate gene roles, and valid identity/candidate
observations. Missing genes use `invalid_input/MISSING_GENES`; a malformed or
non-two-role request uses `invalid_input/INVALID_QUERY_PAIR`. Missing scope is
`invalid_input/MISSING_SCOPE`. Unregistered scope uses `not_found/UNKNOWN_LAYER`
or `not_found/UNKNOWN_MULTIPLEX`. Unavailable explicit direction uses
`invalid_input/DIRECTION_UNAVAILABLE`; a stale cursor uses
`invalid_input/INVALID_CURSOR`. S1 identity statuses retain their meanings under
`UNRESOLVED_IDENTITY`, with the original observation kept as a partial.

Confirmed global absence uses `not_found/NO_MULTIPLEX_MEMBERSHIP`. Keep the
actual unavailable neighbor result or multiplex membership observation as a
partial, including its graph evidence. Unavailable neighbor tuples are unchecked.
Once this blocker is established, do not acquire an unnecessary second list.
The branch omits uncomputed shared IDs and counts.

A known local rejection needs no call and has `rejected_arguments:null`.
A tool rejection supplies the shared empty-provenance `{issue_code, arguments}`
result; copy its exact seven arguments into `rejected_arguments`. A requested
shared-neighbor ranking without a defined rule uses
`ambiguous/SHARED_NEIGHBOR_RANKING_REQUIRED`, preserving the raw request in the
surrounding user turn; no ranked-intersection behavior is invented here.

Ordinary answers omit claim cards. By itself, a complete empty intersection proves only
the absence of a common neighbor for the specified orientations and scope. It
does not prove no direct edge, no longer path, biological noninteraction, or
non-expression. Checked layer absence retains the approved scoped edge/path
permissions for that endpoint; global absence retains its separate prerequisite
meaning. Explicit claim calibration must use the shared closed vocabularies,
subjects, and evidence rules. Native TF directions license recorded roles, not
activation/repression sign or causality.

# S2.8: Degree and Hubness

<a id="s28-review"></a>
> **Review state: approved**, editorial revision `S2.8-r1.1`; human approval recorded
> in `S2-design-r14`, 2026-10-27. The user accepted G1–G6 and directed the
> review to S2.9. All 31 worked traces are retained. Runtime implementation
> and corpus construction remain later work.

## What this family should teach

Answer the requested distinct-neighbor count and, when asked, compare its exact
rank within the declared reference population with the declared hub threshold.
A degree is a count. A percentile is a population-relative statistic. A hub-like
label is a policy decision; none of these alone establishes biological importance,
causality, or a measured effect on proximity.

The ten original question roles remain. Their illustrative degrees, percentiles,
legacy scope strings, provenance, and claim fields are replaced with explicit
semantics and source-derived records. A request for degree alone does not require
a percentile lookup. A known multiplex member absent from the requested layer
has zero neighbors there under the approved S2.3 rule; its rank among that layer's
nodes is unavailable. Preserve that known zero when a hub request must defer.

## Scope, direction, and the counted object

<a id="s28-semantics"></a>
Use the approved typed `LayerScope`: explicit `layers` has a nonempty list of
unique registered IDs in manifest order and `layer_family:null`; `all` has an
empty `layer_ids` list and a null or valid family selector. All-layer and
all-family scopes expand exhaustively against the active manifest. A valid
family with no registered layers expands to an empty scope; an explicitly empty
`layers` selection is invalid. Do not use an omitted argument to mean all layers.

The pinned degree policy is `distinct_neighbor_union_v1`:

| Direction | Set whose cardinality is the degree |
| --- | --- |
| `undirected` | Distinct neighbors in selected undirected layers; unavailable if any selected layer is directed |
| `out` | Distinct targets of query → neighbor across selected directed layers |
| `in` | Distinct sources of neighbor → query across selected directed layers |
| `incident` | Union of both native directions in directed layers and adjacency in undirected layers |

Explicit incoming/outgoing requests require directed representations throughout
the selected scope. A mixed directed/undirected scope can use `incident`, which
defines the meaning of an unqualified degree request. In an undirected scope,
`undirected` is an equivalent operational form. For one undirected layer,
`undirected` and `incident` denote the same set; manifest evidence can establish
that equivalence. The primitive neighbor tool still accepts only `in`, `out`,
and `undirected`; its interface is unchanged.

Deduplicate neighbor IDs across source rows, reciprocal directions, and selected
layers. A retained self-loop contributes the query ID once, including to the
incident union. This is distinct-neighbor degree, not an incidence convention
that counts an undirected self-loop twice. Weights do not enter the count.
Adding per-layer or directional degrees is generally wrong because their sets
may overlap. Complete visible lists or an authoritative union count can establish
the union; separate counts cannot generally do so.

Global membership is the prerequisite for the neighbor operation. A global member
absent from a selected layer contributes no adjacency there. A member present in
one selected layer and absent from another still has a well-defined union degree.
A gene outside the multiplex has unavailable adjacency, not measured degree zero.
No registry filter changes any of these graph sets.

## A declared percentile and hub policy

<a id="s28-rank-policy"></a>
`selected_layer_node_union_v1` defines the reference population as the distinct
union of the authoritative node inventories of the resolved selected layers.
Every member is included, including nodes whose requested directional degree is
zero and graph nodes absent from the registry. Do not rank among only returned
neighbors, positive-degree nodes, illustrated genes, registry-valid genes, or a
filtered target set. Equivalent selectors resolving to the same layers have the
same population. In this source view the inventories are the complete file
endpoint unions. A future source's explicit isolated nodes must also be retained
when its authoritative layer inventory includes them. A multiplex-only isolate
outside every selected layer is outside this population even under `kind:all`.

`degree_midrank_v1` is the proposed percentile policy. It is deliberately named
and pinned because there is no universal percentile definition. For query degree
d, let N be the population size, L the number of members with degree less than d,
and E the number with degree equal to d, including the query. For N > 1:

```text
percentile_exact = 100 * (2*L + E - 1) / (2*(N - 1))
hub_like = 100*(2*L + E - 1) >= threshold_percentile * 2*(N - 1)
```

Equal-degree nodes share the average rank. A unique minimum is 0; a unique maximum
is 100. An all-tied population has percentile 50. For N = 1, this policy explicitly
uses the neutral percentile 50 and compares 50 with the threshold. For N = 0,
or a query outside the population, no percentile or hub classification exists.
These are policy conventions, not additional graph facts. The current four-file
view has no singleton nonempty population; do not invent one in its traces.

Return the exact integer support L, E, N and display `degree_percentile` as the
exact ratio rounded to six decimal places using decimal `ROUND_HALF_UP`, with
insignificant trailing zeros optional in JSON numbers. Classification uses the
exact integer comparison above, never the rounded display. A display of 95.0
at lower precision cannot establish equality with 95. A saved display without
exact support is insufficient near a threshold.

The harness declares the default hub threshold as integer percentile 95.
A visible user/harness override may select an integer from 0 through 100; this
revision does not silently coerce fractional, string, out-of-range, or boolean
thresholds. Thresholds are policy inputs, not measurements from the network.
Equality qualifies as hub-like. Case .3 supplies threshold 100 and a verified
unique maximum, making exact equality real rather than inventing a degree at an
unattainable percentile 95. Case .4 uses the actual nearest attainable PPI rank
below 95, and .29 shows why rounding must not decide classification.

An inclusive cumulative distribution would rank the 5,784 zero-outdegree CD4
nodes at about 99.42, labeling them hubs at 95. The proposed average-rank rule
instead places those tied zeros at about 49.71. Even with this rule, a positive
outdegree of one can rank above 95 in this sparse directed population. Therefore
`hub_like:true` means only that the declared scoped rank meets the declared
threshold; it does not necessarily mean a large absolute degree.

For a computed true label, keep the established caveat token
`high_degree_inflates_apparent_proximity` as a **policy warning** about potential
degree-related proximity bias, not a claim that inflation was measured or must
occur. Its presence does not establish an actual effect, biological importance,
or causality. False or unevaluated labels use `caveats:[]`; an empty caveat list
does not establish that an unperformed hub check was negative.

## Explicit tool and result shapes

<a id="s28-interface"></a>
Identity and scope resolution follow the approved S1/S2 rules. A canonical ID
may go directly to the graph tool; exact registry context can resolve a symbol.
Do not infer symbols from the reviewer source catalogue. This proposed tool has
exactly six arguments:

```text
get_degree({
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_scope: LayerScope,
  gene_id: canonical gene ID,
  direction: incident | in | out | undirected,
  request_kind: degree_only | degree_and_hub,
  hub_policy: null | {
    policy_id: degree_midrank_v1,
    threshold_percentile: integer in [0,100]
  }
})
```

`degree_only` requires `hub_policy:null`; `degree_and_hub` requires the declared
policy and threshold. Degree policy and population policy are pinned by this
interface version and must be returned explicitly for evidence compatibility.
The measurement result has exactly these fields:

```text
DegreeMeasurement: {
  gene_id: canonical gene ID,
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_scope: LayerScope,
  resolved_layer_ids: [registered layer ID, ...],
  direction: incident | in | out | undirected,
  request_kind: degree_only | degree_and_hub,
  degree_policy_id: distinct_neighbor_union_v1,
  membership: {
    present_in_multiplex: boolean,
    present_in_scope: boolean | null
  },
  degree: nonnegative integer | null,
  degree_percentile: number | null,
  rank_support: null | {
    population_policy_id: selected_layer_node_union_v1,
    lower_degree_count: nonnegative integer,
    equal_degree_count: positive integer,
    population_count: positive integer
  },
  hub_policy: HubPolicy | null
}
```

`present_in_scope` means membership in the selected-layer union population,
not presence in every selected layer. It can be null in a derived degree-only
answer if the count is established but narrower membership is not needed or
observed. It is true for a valid percentile record. A confirmed global absence
uses `present_in_multiplex:false`, `present_in_scope:null`, and `degree:null`.
The scope and resolved layer IDs still identify the attempted operation.

A resolved tool result supplies this measurement. A globally present query
outside the reference population returns measured degree 0; for `degree_only`
this resolves, while `degree_and_hub` returns `not_found` with null percentile
and rank support. An empty selected family behaves the same way. A globally
absent query returns `not_found` with null degree. Keep these supported tool
observations as attributed partials in the final diagnostic; do not throw away
known zero or invent rank counts for an excluded query.

The ordinary final `result` is `DegreeMeasurement` plus exactly:

```text
hub_like: boolean | null,
caveats: [high_degree_inflates_apparent_proximity] | []
```

It has no claim cards or generic collection pagination fields. For degree-only,
`degree_percentile`, `rank_support`, `hub_policy`, and `hub_like` are null and
`caveats` is empty because no hub evaluation was requested. For degree-and-hub,
copy the supported degree and exact rank support, calculate or copy the defined
rounded display consistently, and apply the exact threshold comparison. A direct
completed question stops; a completed requested workflow step continues, including
zero or nonhub answers. An unavailable required rank defers.

## Evidence reuse and sufficient calculations

<a id="s28-evidence"></a>
Match the query ID, multiplex/version, resolved layers, requested direction,
and degree policy. A hub evaluation additionally requires compatible population
and percentile policies; degree-only evidence need not contain those statistics. Use visible manifest
metadata to establish selector or direction equivalence; preserve every original
record's scope, data, and evidence ID when deriving an answer. Deduplicate identical
provenance in first-use order. Conflicting counts, weights, membership, rank
support, or evidence-ID reuse are data/harness faults, not reasons to choose a
convenient value.

| Visible compatible evidence | What it supports |
| --- | --- |
| Complete one-layer neighbor set for the requested direction | Exact degree by distinct-ID count; no population rank by itself |
| Bounded or paged list with authoritative non-null full `total_count` | Exact degree despite omitted identities; no need to fetch omitted rows for a count-only question |
| Incomplete list with unknown full total | Only a lower bound; obtain the degree or finish complete retrieval |
| Complete multiplex map or complete native lists covering the scope | Exact union degree after deduplication; no percentile by itself |
| Separate incoming/outgoing or per-layer totals | Generally insufficient for the union; do not add them |
| Matching measurement with exact rank support | Degree and hub evaluation with no graph call |
| Matching exact ranks but a new threshold | Recompare to the new visible threshold without reacquiring the graph |
| Complete compatible degree histogram plus query degree and reference-population membership | Compute L, E, N, percentile, and classification from visible evidence with no extra graph call |
| Rounded percentile alone | Does not substitute for exact support at a threshold |

A histogram record declares the same multiplex/version, typed scope, resolved
layers, direction, degree policy, population policy, population count, complete
ascending `{degree,node_count}` rows, and `complete:true`. Its row counts sum to
N, and all attainable degree values appear exactly once. No hidden construction
oracle supplies a missing population statistic. A histogram plus global membership
alone cannot rank a query in a narrower layer: establish membership in that
reference population. Context for another version or incompatible counting
policy does not become usable by relabeling it.

When a new count lookup is simpler than enumerating a large incomplete list,
`get_degree` may directly establish the missing count. It is not necessary to
exhaust neighbor pages solely to count them. If a complete traversal is used,
follow the approved cursors without changing selection, retain all pages, and
count only after exhaustion. A final page by itself does not prove a complete
set. Required backend failure retains every supported earlier observation,
including an exact degree even when rank acquisition fails.

## Diagnostics and failures

<a id="s28-diagnostics"></a>
A required unrecovered backend failure uses the shared fixed result:

```text
result: {
  failed_tool: string,
  error_code: string,
  arguments: exact failed call arguments,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: null
}
```

This family is one requested statistic, so it does not fabricate a multi-input
coverage partition. Use null coverage and explicitly attributed intermediate
observations. Failed calls add no evidence. Retry only when the visible runtime
message supplies a positive integer `retries_remaining`; repeat the identical tool and arguments, including all six fields for
`get_degree`. Stop after recovery. Exhaustion defers for backend recovery.

An unresolved prerequisite uses this fixed final diagnostic:

```text
result: {
  issue_code: string,
  request: {
    gene: original supplied JSON value | null,
    multiplex_id: string | null,
    layer_scope: original supplied JSON value | null,
    direction: original supplied JSON value | null,
    request_kind: original supplied JSON value | null,
    hub_policy: original supplied JSON value | null
  },
  rejected_arguments: exact DegreeArguments | null,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: null
}
```

Known local rejection needs no call and has `rejected_arguments:null`. A tool
scope/input rejection has empty provenance and the shared `{issue_code,arguments}`
result; preserve its exact arguments in the final diagnostic. Missing gene/scope
uses `invalid_input/MISSING_GENE` or `invalid_input/MISSING_SCOPE`; malformed
selection uses `invalid_input/INVALID_SCOPE`; unavailable explicit direction uses
`invalid_input/DIRECTION_UNAVAILABLE`; unsupported policy or malformed threshold
uses `invalid_input/INVALID_HUB_POLICY`. Unregistered scope uses
`not_found/UNKNOWN_LAYER` or `not_found/UNKNOWN_MULTIPLEX`. Unresolved identity
retains its S1 status under `UNRESOLVED_IDENTITY`, original input, candidates, and
supported partial records; do not guess a candidate or call the graph with one.

A confirmed globally absent query uses `not_found/NO_MULTIPLEX_MEMBERSHIP`.
A known member outside a nonempty selected reference population uses
`not_found/OUTSIDE_REFERENCE_POPULATION` for a required hub evaluation. Any N=0
population, including a valid empty selection, uses `not_found/EMPTY_REFERENCE_POPULATION` for that evaluation.
Both retain known degree 0 and explicit membership evidence as partial data;
these are not ordinary degree-and-hub answers with a fabricated negative label.
A degree-only request in either latter situation resolves zero. None of these
scoped observations establishes no expression, no biological interaction, or
absence in another graph version.

## Real records and attainable sampling

<a id="s28-sources"></a>
Every graph fact below is derived from the unchanged [four-file source view](#shared-fixture),
using full endpoint inventories and native directed edges. The 19,033-node union
is not an induced graph of the illustrated genes. All layer and union populations
retain graph-only IDs. Degree, rank support, and displayed percentiles are
recomputed from these full populations; hub policy is separately declared.
The reviewer catalogue is not automatic model context.

| Verified query/scope | Degree and exact rank support | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PLEKHA4, PPI | 2,940; L=18,000, E=1, N=18,001 | Unique maximum; exact percentile 100 |
| OCIAD1, PPI | 381; L=17,093, E=8, N=18,001 | Nearest attainable PPI percentile below 95 |
| TUBB4A, PPI | 382; L=17,101, E=4, N=18,001 | First attainable PPI percentile above 95 |
| PLEKHA4, all four layers | 2,975; L=19,032, E=1, N=19,033 | Full multiplex distinct union |
| ICAM1, all four layers | 453; L=18,077, E=7, N=19,033 | Exact rank below 95 despite coarse display 95.0 |
| CDC27, outgoing CD4 | 0; L=0, E=5,784, N=5,818 | Present-node zero within a large tie |
| MFRP, PPI and coexpression | Degree 1 in each; union degree 1 | Same neighbor contributes once across layers |
| BCL6, incoming CD4 | Degree 1, the retained self-loop | Self counted once |
| ZBED3, brain TF | Incoming 15, outgoing 29, incident 43 | Reciprocal overlap makes sum 44 wrong |

The review view supplies PPI, coexpression, and two TF-target layers. It has no
registered bulk PEN, single-cell PEN, or other-family layer, and no separate
full-layer isolate inventory. The empty-family example demonstrates selector
semantics, not real PEN biology. Do not fabricate those families or isolates.
The displayed query identities and the supplied TUBB4A symbol were verified
against the pinned registry index and original Ensembl 116 GTF. Graph neighbors
remain valid even without a registry mapping.

<a id="s28-sampling"></a>
Apply the approved [attainable-range policy](#s22-sampling) to degree values,
reference-population sizes, ties, ranks relative to the threshold, layer subset
sizes, directions, and membership patterns. Sample from the full attainable
source-derived domains with equal weight across attainable count strata by
default, then sample records within a stratum. Report conditioning and any
budget-driven departures. Do not let a few examples define the production
range, invent unattainable percentiles to hit a threshold, or silently drop
high-degree strata to fit context.

Sample below/equal/above threshold cases only where attainable for the declared
policy, and use explicit policy overrides when appropriate. Include zero ties,
positive ties, source-present directional zeros, absent-layer zeros, empty scopes,
self-loops, reciprocal overlap, cross-layer overlap, multiple selected layers,
equivalent selectors, incompatible context, and registry-independent membership.
Recompute statistics for each actual graph version, eligible scope, direction,
and split policy. All-layer populations and percentile histograms must use full
authoritative source inventories, not train-only target subsets.

Degree-only and degree-and-hub questions, direct and workflow framing, enough
context and missing evidence, success and failure, and different threshold
policies must vary independently. Use at least 32 reviewed wrappers per framing
with content independent of wording-bank size; freeze held-out panels and inputs.
Use actual tokenizer/context-budget checks without a hard reasoning prose cap.
Large neighbor lists need an explicit count/statistic or pagination strategy,
not hidden truncation. Source pins, policy versions, seeds, attainable domains,
and sampling histograms belong in construction records. Runtime, contract,
corpora, and queued jobs remain unchanged during this design review.
