# S2.9: Induced Subgraph

<a id="s29-review"></a>
> **Review state: in_review**, revision `S2.9-r1` in `S2-design-r14`,
> 2026-10-27. The user approved S2.8 and directed the review here. This is
> a design-document proposal; runtime implementation and corpus construction
> remain later work.

## What this family should teach

Classify every requested canonical gene in one registered layer, then return the
native edges whose two endpoints belong to the layer-member subset. This default
projection is a complete answer even when some requested IDs are outside the
layer or multiplex. Excluded inputs retain their explicit membership categories;
they do not become fabricated isolated nodes or evaluated negative edge queries.

The six original question roles remain. Their illustrative graph facts are
replaced with verified source sets and exact weights. In particular, a source
check found that the legacy proposed PPI isolate actually connects to another
selected node, and the legacy TF example had incorrect membership and edges.
Preserve the intended roles using the replacement fixtures listed below, rather
than treating those original numbers or selected identities as authoritative.

A selected node with no incident edge inside the complete projected set remains
in `layer_gene_ids`. Isolation inside that set does not mean isolation in the
whole layer. An incomplete edge display alone does not establish isolation by omission.
Independent complete incidence evidence can still establish it. A singleton
can have a self-loop. An explicit empty request or a complete classification
with no projected layer members gives an empty edge domain without edge lookup.

## Input, projection, native direction, and ordering

<a id="s29-semantics"></a>
Resolve symbols and noncanonical IDs under the approved S1 identity rules. Keep
raw lookup arguments, candidate sets, returned canonical IDs, null symbols,
and supplied identity evidence. A canonical ID can go directly to the graph
operation. Registry validity does not establish graph membership, and graph
membership does not justify an invented symbol. Do not guess an unresolved
identity or expand an ambiguous input into all its candidates.

After identity resolution, deduplicate canonical IDs in first-mention order.
Use that order in tool `gene_ids` and membership coverage. Keep the original
spellings, order, and duplicates in the user request and diagnostic request.
The three result categories are sorted ascending by ID and partition exactly
these unique inputs:

- `layer_gene_ids`: requested members of the selected layer, including nodes
  with no incident edge inside the induced set.
- `not_in_layer_gene_ids`: requested multiplex members absent from that layer.
- `missing_gene_ids`: requested IDs absent from the multiplex; these are not
  also placed in the layer-absence category.

Use the authoritative full layer inventories approved in S2.5/S2.6. For this
view, each inventory is the union of both complete source endpoint columns.
Target-only directed nodes belong to the layer. Retain graph-only IDs without
registry filtering. A future authoritative inventory may contain full-layer
isolates, but this review view has no separate isolated-node inventory.

This family selects exactly one registered layer, not a layer family or a union.
Valid syntax does not establish registration. The active manifest supplies native
`directed` metadata. No traversal-direction argument is needed: an induced
native graph contains every recorded ordered arc between its selected members
when the layer is directed, and every unordered edge when it is undirected.
An incoming arc does not disappear because the user mentioned its target first.

Each edge is `{gene_ids:[endpoint_1,endpoint_2],weight:number}`. In an undirected
layer sort the pair ascending; in a directed layer keep `[source,target]` in
native order. Sort the list lexicographically by that endpoint tuple. Preserve
reciprocal arcs as distinct rows with their own weights. A retained self-loop
appears once as `[gene_id,gene_id]`; it is not deleted or doubled. The pinned
source descriptor rejects duplicate native source keys. Deduplicate repeated
identical observations across pages or context, and reject conflicting weights
for one native key as data faults.
Do not average, normalize, round, rescale, or infer weights from other layers.

## Tool and ordinary result

<a id="s29-interface"></a>
The proposed single-layer tool has exactly six required arguments:

```text
induce_subgraph({
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: registered layer ID,
  gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  mode: complete | top_k,
  top_k: positive integer | null,
  cursor: string | null
})
```

`complete` requires `top_k:null`. `top_k` requests the first K native edge tuples
in the canonical order above and requires a positive integer K. This is an
explicit **edge preview**, not strongest-weight ranking and not automatically
a complete induced graph. An ordinary request for the induced subgraph uses
complete mode. An unspecified strongest/ranked preview needs clarification of
its ranking rule; this revision does not invent one. K greater than the full
edge count returns all edges and can complete the collection. Do not silently
impose an unrequested bound or interpret `top_k:0` as an empty request.

The exact successful tool result and ordinary final result are:

```text
result: {
  multiplex_id: string,
  layer_id: string,
  directed: boolean,
  layer_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  layer_gene_count: nonnegative integer,
  not_in_layer_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  missing_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
  edges: [{gene_ids:[canonical gene ID,canonical gene ID],weight:number}, ...],
  edge_count: nonnegative integer,
  coverage: {
    operation: layer_membership,
    requested_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
    checked_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...],
    unchecked_gene_ids: [canonical gene ID, ...]
  },
  collection: {
    mode: complete | top_k,
    returned_count: nonnegative integer,
    total_count: nonnegative integer | null,
    complete: boolean,
    next_cursor: string | null
  }
}
```

`layer_gene_count` is the size of the full selected layer-member subset.
`edge_count` and `collection.returned_count` both equal the number of edge rows
in this response or assembled final answer. `collection.total_count` is the full
number of induced native edges, not the number of layer nodes and not the full
layer's edge count. Preserve null when that total is unknown. A completed
complete result has all three edge counts equal and `complete:true`.

**Membership coverage and edge completeness are separate.** Every successful
response, including an edge page or bounded preview, supplies the full three-way
classification and checked coverage for all unique requested IDs. Repeat that
classification unchanged on later edge pages. A successful page may have every
membership input checked while its edge collection is incomplete. These are not
claims that all edge predicates or full neighborhoods were acquired.

Default projection resolves mixed exclusions, all-excluded inputs, an empty edge
set, and a nonempty graph. A direct completed request stops; a completed requested
workflow step continues. If the user explicitly requires every requested gene
to be a layer member before proceeding, treat that as a separate visible gate:
retain the complete classification as partial evidence and defer if it fails.
Do not silently add that prerequisite to ordinary projection questions.

An explicitly supplied empty gene list is valid once the multiplex, layer, and
native directedness are established. It needs no graph call: all categories,
edges, and coverage are empty; all counts are zero; provenance is empty. It says
nothing about the layer's overall node or edge counts. Missing or null input is
not the explicit empty set and uses the diagnostic branch. A singleton still
needs evidence about its membership and possible self-loop.

## Complete evidence and reuse

<a id="s29-evidence"></a>
Match the canonical input IDs, multiplex, graph version, layer, and native
representation. Preserve original acquisition arguments, scopes, data, and
evidence IDs when restricting or combining records. Deduplicate supporting
provenance in first-use order. A positive edge establishes membership of its
endpoints. A resolved native neighbor record with both absence lists empty
establishes query layer membership even when its directional list is empty.
A complete empty record with the query in its layer-absence list instead
establishes that scoped absence, not layer membership. A global-negative observation can classify
an excluded input, even if its own neighbor operation returned `not_found`.
It does not turn that unavailable neighbor operation into a successful edge check.

An exact projected graph needs the complete membership partition and a sufficient
proof for every possible native edge among the layer members, including loops.
For n projected nodes, there are n² directed ordered candidate pairs or n(n+1)/2
undirected candidate pairs with replacement. These are proof domains, not extra
quadratic arrays required in the response.

| Compatible visible evidence | Sufficient conclusion or remaining work |
| --- | --- |
| Complete induced graph for the same input set | Reuse the full answer, with coverage reordered to the current request |
| Complete induced graph for a superset of requested inputs | Restrict all three categories and both endpoints of each edge, then recompute counts |
| Complete outgoing lists for every projected node in a directed layer | Every ordered pair, including each self-loop, is settled; incoming lists are unnecessary |
| Complete incoming lists for every projected node in a directed layer | The same completeness follows using target roles |
| Complete undirected lists for every projected node | Keep only selected endpoints and write each edge once |
| Records for only some inputs | Reuse their facts; complete only missing membership and candidate-pair/loop proofs |
| Incomplete lists with positive edges | Keep those positives, but omissions remain unknown unless another sufficient observation covers them |
| One observed self-loop for an established singleton member | That is its only candidate pair, so its complete singleton graph is known even if the original neighbor list is incomplete |
| Full membership partition but no edge evidence | This alone is generally insufficient to induce a nonempty member set |

For directed (u,v), a complete outgoing list of u or a complete incoming list of
v settles that pair. For undirected {u,v}, a complete list of either endpoint
settles the pair. An unqueried member's own self-loop still needs support; do not
assume the absence of loops from the absence of another edge. A complete input
partition with no layer members makes the projected edge domain empty without
any neighbor calls. Other candidate-by-candidate proofs can be sufficient when
all required membership, negative/positive edge facts, and weights are visible.
The approved S2.1 `get_edge` tool requires distinct endpoints; do not invent a
self-pair call to it. Loop evidence can come from native neighbor or subgraph
records.

A saved proper-subset graph cannot generally establish newly added nodes or
cross-edges. In particular, inducing separately on disjoint input batches and
unioning their results misses cross-batch edges. A decomposition is valid only
with an explicit complete proof covering all cross-batch pairs and loops.
S2.6's independent membership-batching rule does not authorize this graph
shortcut. Case .29 shows two edgeless singleton subgraphs whose combined set
has a real edge.

A bounded edge prefix can answer the same or a shorter explicit preview for the
same selected input set. It generally cannot answer a complete request, a larger
prefix, or a new node selection without sufficient additional evidence. An
omitted edge is not a negative and an unconnected displayed node is not proven
isolated. State the proof when unusually sufficient partial evidence does settle
the complete graph; do not require every full neighborhood by rote.

## Edge pagination, failures, and prerequisites

<a id="s29-diagnostics"></a>
Start a new selection with `cursor:null`. Follow returned cursors exactly,
keeping the entire first-mention-ordered deduplicated `gene_ids`, layer, mode,
K, and graph version unchanged. Pagination partitions the **edge rows**, not the
input gene set. Retain every successful page and its evidence, require identical
membership partitions, deduplicate identical edge keys, and reject inconsistent
weights, totals, direction metadata, or classifications.

A last page can be incomplete by itself. A complete final answer accumulates the
whole traversal from its initial cursor through exhaustion, then calculates the
unique edge count if no authoritative full total was supplied. Check non-null
totals against that accumulation. In top-K mode exhaustion completes only the
requested preview unless separate metadata establishes the full collection.
A partial page record can still supply a specific positive fact without proving
the rest of the traversal. Starting a different selection requires a null cursor;
never invent or repurpose a cursor.

An unrecovered required lookup uses the shared failure shape:

```text
result: {
  failed_tool: string,
  error_code: string,
  arguments: exact failed tool arguments,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: GeneMembershipCoverage | null
}
```

Retain exact successful registry, membership, neighbor, and edge-page observations.
Membership coverage refers to the outer canonical input list and selected layer;
checked/unchecked inputs form a disjoint partition in first-mention order. It
may be fully checked when edge retrieval is still incomplete. Use null when a
valid graph scope or canonical input domain is not established. Do not return an
ordinary graph with empty placeholders after an edge failure. Failed calls add
no evidence. A supported partial edge count remains a count of shown edges,
not an exact full induced-edge count unless independently established.

Retry only when the visible runtime message supplies a positive integer
`retries_remaining`. Repeat the identical tool and arguments, including the
six subgraph fields and exact cursor when applicable. Stop after recovery;
a terminal or exhausted failure defers for backend recovery. A checked absence
or a missing-identity result does not authorize a retry.

Other unresolved prerequisites use this fixed diagnostic shape:

```text
result: {
  issue_code: string,
  request: {
    genes: original supplied JSON value | null,
    multiplex_id: string | null,
    layer_id: string | null,
    mode: original supplied JSON value | null,
    top_k: original supplied JSON value | null,
    cursor: original supplied JSON value | null,
    require_all_in_layer: boolean
  },
  rejected_arguments: exact SubgraphArguments | null,
  partial_results: [PartialResult, ...],
  coverage: GeneMembershipCoverage | null
}
```

Local rejection needs no call and has `rejected_arguments:null`. Tool rejections
use the shared empty-provenance `{issue_code,arguments}` result; retain the exact
six rejected subgraph arguments in the final diagnostic. Missing scope is
`invalid_input/MISSING_SCOPE`; missing genes are `invalid_input/MISSING_GENES`;
invalid list shape is `invalid_input/INVALID_GENE_LIST`. Invalid mode/K or cursor
uses `invalid_input/INVALID_SELECTION` or `invalid_input/INVALID_CURSOR`.
Unregistered scope uses `not_found/UNKNOWN_LAYER` or `not_found/UNKNOWN_MULTIPLEX`.
Unresolved identity retains its S1 status under `UNRESOLVED_IDENTITY`, with the
literal input and original identity response as a partial. It is not graph
absence. An explicit unmet all-members gate uses
`not_found/MEMBERSHIP_PRECONDITION_UNSATISFIED`, retaining the actual partition.
Weight-ranked selections require a separately defined interface and selection
rule; do not silently substitute the canonical prefix. Native projection does
not create an undirected
collapse or weight aggregation rule for a directed layer.

Ordinary answers omit claim cards. A complete empty induced graph supports no
recorded edge **within the projected selected-member set in this layer/version**.
It does not establish no longer path through other nodes, no interaction in
biology, non-expression, or absence in another context. Preserve the approved
scoped claim permissions for separately checked layer/global absence. A missing
global node was excluded from projection, not subjected to an available edge
predicate. Native TF arcs support recorded direction, not activation/repression,
causality, or physical binding inferred from a positive weight.

## Real source roles and attainable sampling

<a id="s29-sources"></a>
The [four-file source view](#shared-fixture), version, source pins, native
directions, and full endpoint inventories remain unchanged. All edge rows and
weights below come from those complete files; no induced fixture is passed off
as the whole network. Pagination boundaries, retry budgets, outages, and
incompatible metadata are injected harness scenarios, not historical backend
captures. The reviewer source catalogue is not automatic model context.

| Original role retained | Verified replacement selection | Source result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| .1 Mixed layer/global exclusions, direct | CDC27, EPOR, GYPE, CETN3, NFYA, CCT8L1P in coexpression | Four members and four edges; NFYA is outside the layer, CCT8L1P outside the multiplex |
| .2 All members with a selected-set isolate, workflow | APP, MAPT, SNCA, MFRP in PPI | Three edges among the first three; MFRP retained as an isolated node in this selected graph |
| .3 No edges among selected members, direct | GFAP, BAX, MFRP in PPI | Three layer members, zero induced edges |
| .4 Supplied symbols, workflow | TP53, CCN5, CHIT1, MDM2 in brain TF | TP53 → CCN5 and TP53 → CHIT1; MDM2 remains in the selected node set |
| .5 Complete neighbor context, direct/no-call | MFRP, C1QTNF5, CDC27 in coexpression | One induced edge; full context contains five neighbor rows |
| .6 Incomplete input evidence, workflow | Same three IDs, only MFRP/C1QTNF5 neighbor context | CDC27 membership and its self-loop remain unobserved until further acquisition |

Other verified contrasts use NFYA ↔ KLF3 in brain TF with distinct weights
0.858361181 and 0.847555996; the CD4 BCL6 self-loop; and a one-way brain TF
TP53 → CCN5 arc whose source ID sorts after its target ID. These examples expose
loss of native direction from blindly sorting endpoints. All display weights
retain source precision. Query and displayed neighbor identities are checked
against the pinned registry and original Ensembl 116 GTF; keep any real graph
ID without a registry mapping rather than dropping it.

<a id="s29-sampling"></a>
Apply the approved [attainable-range policy](#s22-sampling) to request sizes,
positive/outside-layer/outside-global counts, projected node counts, induced
edge counts, selected-set isolation, self-loops, and reciprocal structure.
Sample genuine source-derived input sets across attainable membership and edge
strata, giving attainable count strata equal weight by default before sampling
sets within them. Pin sources, seeds, population/domain definitions, and observed
sampling histograms. Disclose conditioning and context-budget departures.

The attainable edge counts depend on layer, actual requested-set size, selected
membership composition, and graph structure. Do not claim that the complete
combinatorial distribution of all possible induced subsets was enumerated.
Use verified sampled domains and targeted source constructions, report gaps,
and never invent edges or unattainable integer counts to fill a bin. Vary input
order and duplicates independently of membership/edge outcomes. Sample preview
K below, equal to, and above actual edge totals where attainable.

The review view contains PPI, coexpression, and two TF-target layers; it has no
registered bulk PEN, single-cell PEN, or other-family layer. Do not fabricate
those representations or full-layer isolates. Production coverage must revisit
all six family meanings with actual eligible sources, rather than treating this
four-layer view as a permanent corpus ceiling. Preserve direction, graph-only
nodes, native edge weights, and all requested inputs.

Use at least 32 reviewed wrappers per framing with content independent of bank
size. Separate direct completion from workflow continuation and explicit gates.
Do not score free-text summaries token for token. Retain evidence-grounded
reasoning with actual tokenizer/context-budget checks and no hard prose cap.
Large graphs need real edge pagination or a declared bounded preview; silently
removing high-count strata or cross-batch edges is not a budget strategy.
Runtime, shared contract, corpora, frozen held-out panels, and queued jobs remain

S2.10: Connected Components

Overall guidance

\* Tool  
  \* induce\_subgraph (S2.9) for the set in one layer, then join the genes that share an edge  
  \* A subgraph record for the same layer that covers the asked genes answers without a call  
\* Components use the set's own edges only  
  \* A path through a gene outside the set does not join two components  
  \* A node with no edge inside the set is a component by itself  
  \* So a split does not show that the genes have no path in the layer  
\* The answer  
  \* The three gene lists of S2.6; genes outside the layer or the multiplex are in no component  
  \* Each component in ascending ID order; components ordered by their first ID; component\_count is the number of components  
  \* single\_component is true exactly when every asked gene is a node in the layer and they form 1 component  
\* Claims  
  \* null when single\_component is true; otherwise set, with the gene-list claims only  
  \* no\_path\_recorded\_in\_scope is never allowed: the components show no path search  
\* Values are illustrative  
  \* Gene IDs and layer tags are real; edge records come from a fixture and must be filled from the full\_brain\_multiplex\_v1 store before these traces become golden

# S2.11: Calibration (No Edge and No Path)

> Review state: pending. This family has not been migrated to
> [S2-design-r1](#shared-review-r1); its existing payloads are not R1-conforming.

S2.11: No Edge and No Path

Overall guidance

\* Tool  
  \* shortest\_path for a pair in one layer: an unweighted search with no hop limit  
  \* gene\_ids copy the task's genes in the task's order; the tool returns them in ascending ID order and gives the path from the lower ID  
\* What the search shows  
  \* No path: the layer records no edge and no path, since a direct edge is a path of 1 hop  
  \* A path of 2 or more hops: the layer records a path but no direct edge  
  \* A path of 1 hop is the edge itself; that question belongs to S2.1  
\* What it does not show  
  \* The absence holds for this layer and this graph version only  
  \* It does not show that the genes are unrelated, that they do not interact, or that the absence holds in other layers  
  \* For a PEN layer, a gene that is not a node does not show that the gene is not expressed  
\* The answer  
  \* path\_found and hop\_count; the path itself is left to the path tasks of S3  
  \* No path, or a gene that is not a node in the layer, is resolved  
  \* A gene that is not in the multiplex is not\_found and defers  
\* Claims  
  \* No path: no\_edge\_recorded\_in\_scope and no\_path\_recorded\_in\_scope, plus gene\_not\_node\_in\_layer when a gene is outside the layer  
  \* A path of 2 or more hops: no\_edge\_recorded\_in\_scope only; a path of 1 hop: null  
  \* A gene outside the multiplex: gene\_not\_node\_in\_multiplex only  
  \* A claim stated in the task goes in claim; claim\_supported is true exactly when it is in allowed\_claims. Both are null when the task states no claim  
\* Records already in context  
  \* An edge record that shows no edge does not show no path: call shortest\_path  
\* Values are illustrative  
  \* Gene IDs and layer tags are real; edge records come from a fixture and must be filled from the full\_brain\_multiplex\_v1 store before these traces become golden

# S2.12: Calibration (Gene Absent from Layer)

> Review state: pending. This family has not been migrated to
> [S2-design-r1](#shared-review-r1); its existing payloads are not R1-conforming.

S2.12: Gene Absent from a Layer

Overall guidance

\* Every task states one claim about one gene and one layer  
  \* The model checks whether the gene is a node in the layer and says whether the claim is supported  
  \* Layer-value tasks for a gene outside the layer (neighbors, degree, shared neighbors) stay in S2.3, S2.4, S2.7, and S2.8, where they defer  
\* Tool  
  \* get\_nodes\_by\_layer for the gene alone (a set of one, as in S2.6)  
\* What the absence shows  
  \* A node of the multiplex with no edge in the layer: gene\_not\_node\_in\_layer  
  \* A gene outside the multiplex: gene\_not\_node\_in\_multiplex  
  \* It does not show that the gene is not expressed in the layer's context, that it is absent from other layers, or that it will be absent from later graph versions  
\* The answer  
  \* node\_in\_layer and missing\_gene\_ids, then claim and claim\_supported  
  \* Claim lists: null when the gene is a node in the layer; otherwise the one allowed claim above  
  \* claim\_supported is true exactly when the claim is in allowed\_claims  
  \* Every answer is resolved, as membership is an existence question (S2.6)  
\* Records already in context  
  \* A gene layer record for the gene, complete or filtered to the layer's family, answers without a call  
  \* A record filtered to another family does not: call get\_nodes\_by\_layer  
\* Values are illustrative  
  \* Gene IDs and layer tags are real; node status comes from a fixture and must be filled from the full\_brain\_multiplex\_v1 store before these traces become golden

S2.11: No Edge and No Path

Overall guidance

\* Tool  
  \* shortest\_path for a pair in one layer: an unweighted search with no hop limit  
  \* gene\_ids copy the task's genes in the task's order; the tool returns them in ascending ID order and gives the path from the lower ID  
\* What the search shows  
  \* No path: the layer records no edge and no path, since a direct edge is a path of 1 hop  
  \* A path of 2 or more hops: the layer records a path but no direct edge  
  \* A path of 1 hop is the edge itself; that question belongs to S2.1  
\* What it does not show  
  \* The absence holds for this layer and this graph version only  
  \* It does not show that the genes are unrelated, that they do not interact, or that the absence holds in other layers  
  \* For a PEN layer, a gene that is not a node does not show that the gene is not expressed  
\* The answer  
  \* path\_found and hop\_count; the path itself is left to the path tasks of S3  
  \* No path, or a gene that is not a node in the layer, is resolved  
  \* A gene that is not in the multiplex is not\_found and defers  
\* Claims  
  \* No path: no\_edge\_recorded\_in\_scope and no\_path\_recorded\_in\_scope, plus gene\_not\_node\_in\_layer when a gene is outside the layer  
  \* A path of 2 or more hops: no\_edge\_recorded\_in\_scope only; a path of 1 hop: null  
  \* A gene outside the multiplex: gene\_not\_node\_in\_multiplex only  
  \* A claim stated in the task goes in claim; claim\_supported is true exactly when it is in allowed\_claims. Both are null when the task states no claim  
\* Records already in context  
  \* An edge record that shows no edge does not show no path: call shortest\_path  
\* Values are illustrative  
  \* Gene IDs and layer tags are real; edge records come from a fixture and must be filled from the full\_brain\_multiplex\_v1 store before these traces become golden
